title.en: Volume 221 Biographies 8: Princes 7: Gao Zongzhuzi, Ren Zong Zhu Zi, Xuan Zongzhuzi, Wen Zongzi
title.raw: 卷221 列傳八 诸王七 高宗诸子 仁宗诸子 宣宗诸子 文宗子

sentences.zh: 諸王七

translations.literal: Princes 7
translations.idiomatic: Princes 7

sentences.zh: 高宗十七子：孝賢純皇后生端慧太子永璉、哲親王永琮，皇后納喇氏生貝勒永璂、永璟，孝儀純皇后生永璐、仁宗、第十六子、慶僖親王永璘，純惠皇貴妃蘇佳氏生循郡王永璋、質莊親王永瑢，哲憫皇貴妃富察氏生定安親王永璜，淑嘉皇貴妃金佳氏生履端親王永珹、儀慎親王永璇、第九子、成哲親王永瑆，愉貴妃珂里葉特氏生榮純親王永琪，舒妃葉赫納喇氏生第十子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had seventeen sons: Empress Xiaoxian Chun bore the Duanhui Crown Prince Yonglian and Prince Zhe Yongzong; Empress Nara bore Beile Yongji and Yongjing; Empress Xiaoyi Chun bore Yonglu, the future Emperor Renzong, the sixteenth son, and Prince Qingxi Yonglin; Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui Su bore Prince Xun Yongzhang and Prince Zhizhuang Yongying; Imperial Noble Consort Zhemin Fu bore Prince Ding'an Yonghuang; Imperial Noble Consort Shujia Jin bore Prince Luduan Yongyi, Prince Yishen Yongxuan, the ninth son, and Prince Chengzhe Yongrong; Imperial Concubine Yu of the Kerilet bore Prince Rongchun Yongqi; Consort Shu of the Yehe Nara bore the tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong fathered seventeen sons. Empress Xiaoxian Chun gave birth to Crown Prince Duanhui Yonglian and Prince Zhe Yongzong. Empress Nara bore Beile Yongji and Yongjing. Empress Xiaoyi Chun bore Yonglu, the man who would become Emperor Renzong, a sixteenth son, and Prince Qingxi Yonglin. Imperial Noble Consort Chunhui of the Su clan bore Prince Xun Yongzhang and Prince Zhizhuang Yongying. Imperial Noble Consort Zhemin of the Fu clan bore Prince Ding'an Yonghuang. Imperial Noble Consort Shujia of the Jin clan bore Prince Luduan Yongyi, Prince Yishen Yongxuan, a ninth son, and Prince Chengzhe Yongrong. Imperial Concubine Yu of the Kerilet clan bore Prince Rongchun Yongqi. Consort Shu of the Yehe Nara clan bore a tenth son.

sentences.zh: 永珹出為履懿親王允祹後，永瑢出為慎靖郡王允禧後。

translations.literal: Yongyi was given out as heir to Prince Luyi Yunxiang, and Yongying as heir to Prince Shenjing Yunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyi was adopted as heir to Prince Luyi Yunxiang, and Yongying as heir to Prince Shenjing Yunxi.

sentences.zh: 永璟、永璐、第九子、第十子、第十六子皆殤，無封。

translations.literal: Yongjing, Yonglu, the ninth son, the tenth son, and the sixteenth son all died young and received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjing, Yonglu, the ninth son, the tenth son, and the sixteenth son all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 定安親王永璜，高宗第一子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding'an Yonghuang was Emperor Gaozong's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding'an Yonghuang was Gaozong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，上南巡，還蹕次德州，孝賢純皇后崩，永璜迎喪，高宗斥其不知禮，切責之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, when the emperor was on a southern tour and halted on the return journey at Dezhou, Empress Xiaoxian Chun died. Yonghuang met the funeral train; Emperor Gaozong rebuked him for not knowing ritual and sharply reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13, while the emperor was on a southern tour, the returning procession halted at Dezhou upon the death of Empress Xiaoxian Chun. Yonghuang went out to meet the funeral cortege, but Gaozong denounced his breach of propriety and rebuked him severely.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「皇長子誕自青宮，齒序居長。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "The eldest imperial son was born in the Eastern Palace and ranks first in seniority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "The eldest imperial son was born in the Eastern Palace and stands first in line among the princes.

sentences.zh: 年逾弱冠，誕毓皇孫。

translations.literal: He had passed the age of twenty and had begotten imperial grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He was already past twenty and had fathered imperial grandsons.

sentences.zh: 今遘疾薨逝，朕心悲悼，宜備成人之禮。」

translations.literal: Now, seized by illness, he has died. My heart grieves; the full rites for an adult should be observed."
translations.idiomatic: Now illness has taken him, and my heart mourns. The full funeral rites owed an adult should be performed."

sentences.zh: 追封定親王，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ding, with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Prince of Ding, with the temple name An.

sentences.zh: 子綿德，襲郡王。

translations.literal: His son Miande inherited the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Miande succeeded to the princedom of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: For an offense he was deprived of his title.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his title after being convicted of an offense.

sentences.zh: 弟綿恩，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mian'en inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mian'en succeeded in his place.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，進封親王。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, he was advanced to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he was promoted to full prince.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年正月，封其子奕紹為不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jiaqing, his son Yishao was enfeoffed as a buluo-fen auxiliary state duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaqing 4 his son Yishao was created an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 八年閏二月，有陳德者，匿禁門，犯蹕，諸王大臣捍禦。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the eighth year, a man named Chen De hid at the forbidden gate, violated the imperial progress, and the princes and great ministers defended against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of the eighth year, a man named Chen De concealed himself at the palace gate and rushed the imperial procession; princes and high ministers fought him off.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜綿恩御用補褂，進奕紹貝子。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed: Mian'en was granted an imperial supplementary jacket, and Yishao was advanced to beile.
translations.idiomatic: For their service, Mian'en was awarded an imperial supplementary jacket and Yishao was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授御前大臣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was appointed an imperial presence minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed a minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，薨，賜銀五千治喪，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he died; five thousand taels of silver were granted for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 2. Five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he received the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子奕紹，先以上六十萬壽進貝勒，至是襲親王。

translations.literal: His son Yishao had earlier, on the emperor's sixtieth birthday, been advanced to beile; now he inherited the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yishao had earlier been promoted to beile on the emperor's sixtieth birthday; he now succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 十五年，奕紹年六十，封其子​​載銓為輔國公。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when Yishao reached sixty, his son Zaiquan was enfeoffed as auxiliary state duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when Yishao turned sixty, his son Zaiquan was created auxiliary state duke.

sentences.zh: 十六年，奕紹薨，賜銀治喪，諡曰端。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yishao died; silver was granted for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Duan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Yishao died. Silver was granted for his funeral, and he received the posthumous name Duan.

sentences.zh: 載銓襲。

translations.literal: Zaiquan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiquan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 載銓初封二等輔國將軍，三進封輔國公，授御前大臣、工部尚書、步軍統領，襲爵。

translations.literal: Zaiquan was first enfeoffed as a second-rank auxiliary state general, thrice advanced to auxiliary state duke, appointed imperial presence minister, Minister of Works, and metropolitan commandant of the infantry, and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiquan was first created a second-rank auxiliary state general, was promoted three times to auxiliary state duke, and was appointed minister in attendance, Minister of Works, and metropolitan infantry commandant before succeeding to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 道光末，受顧命。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign, he received the imperial deathbed charge.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daoguang reign he was named to the regency council on the emperor's deathbed.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，益用事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he wielded power all the more.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong took the throne, his influence grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年六月，給事中袁甲三疏劾：「載銓營私舞弊，自謂'操進退用人之權'。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xianfeng, the supervising secretary Yuan Jiasan memorialized in impeachment: "Zaiquan schemes for private gain and commits fraud, claiming for himself 'the power to advance, retire, and appoint men.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xianfeng 2 the supervising secretary Yuan Jiasan impeached him in a memorial: "Zaiquan pursues private profit and bends the rules, boasting that he holds 'the power to promote, dismiss, and appoint officials.'

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書恆春、侍郎書元潛赴私邸，聽其指使。

translations.literal: The Minister of Punishments Hengchun and Vice Minister Shuyuan secretly went to his private residence and obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Hengchun and Vice Minister Shuyuan secretly visited his private mansion and took orders from him.

sentences.zh: 步軍統領衙門但準收呈，例不審辦；

translations.literal: The metropolitan infantry commandant's office was by regulation only to receive petitions and not to try cases;
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the metropolitan infantry commandant's office was only to accept petitions, not to adjudicate cases;

sentences.zh: 而載銓不識大體，任意顛倒，遇有盜案諮部，乃以武斷濟其規避。

translations.literal: yet Zaiquan did not understand the larger principle, arbitrarily reversed decisions, and when theft cases were referred to the ministry, used arbitrary judgment to help evade them.
translations.idiomatic: yet Zaiquan showed no sense of the larger interest, capriciously reversed rulings, and when theft cases were referred to the ministry used arbitrary power to help parties evade justice.

sentences.zh: 又廣收門生，外間傳聞有定門四配、十哲、七十二賢之稱。」

translations.literal: He also widely took disciples; outside it was rumored that he had the 'Four Associates,' 'Ten Wise Ones,' and 'Seventy-two Worthies' of a fixed school."
translations.idiomatic: He also took disciples on a grand scale, and rumor abroad compared his circle to Confucius's Four Associates, Ten Wise Ones, and Seventy-two Disciples."

sentences.zh: 舉所繪息肩圖朝官題詠有師生稱謂為證。

translations.literal: He cited as proof the teacher-and-disciple terms in court officials' poems inscribed on the painted Resting-the-Shoulders scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He offered as evidence the teacher-and-pupil language in court officials' inscriptions on the painted Resting-the-Shoulders scroll.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「諸王與在廷臣工不得往來，歷聖垂誡周詳。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "Princes and officials at court must not associate; successive emperors have left thorough admonitions on this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "Princes and officials at court must not mingle; successive emperors have left explicit warnings on the point.

sentences.zh: 恆春、書元因審辦案件，趨府私謁，載銓並未拒絕。

translations.literal: Hengchun and Shuyuan, because of cases under review, went to his mansion on private visits, and Zaiquan did not refuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Because of cases under review, Hengchun and Shuyuan paid private calls at his mansion, and Zaiquan did not turn them away.

sentences.zh: 至拜認師生，例有明禁，而息肩圖題詠中，載齡、許誦恆均以門生自居，不知遠嫌。」

translations.literal: As for acknowledging teacher and disciple, there is a clear prohibition; yet in the inscriptions on the Resting-the-Shoulders scroll, Zailing and Xu Songheng each styled themselves disciples, not knowing to keep their distance."
translations.idiomatic: Acknowledging a teacher-disciple bond is expressly forbidden, yet in the Resting-the-Shoulders inscriptions Zailing and Xu Songheng each called themselves his pupils, showing no sense of propriety."

sentences.zh: 罰王俸二年，所領職並罷。

translations.literal: He was fined two years of princely stipend and stripped of all offices held.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined two years of princely stipend and dismissed from every post he held.

sentences.zh: 九月，仍授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was again appointed metropolitan commandant of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was reappointed metropolitan infantry commandant.

sentences.zh: 三年，加親王銜，充辦理巡防事宜。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the rank of prince of the first rank and appointed to manage patrol and defense affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was granted princely rank and charged with managing patrol and defense affairs.

sentences.zh: 二月，疏請申明會議舊章，報可。

translations.literal: In the second month he memorialized asking that the old regulations on council deliberation be clarified; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he memorialized to clarify the old rules on council deliberation, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，病作，詔以綿德曾孫溥煦為後。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, when illness set in, an edict named Miande's great-grandson Puxu as heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year, as illness took hold, an edict named Miande's great-grandson Puxu as his heir.

sentences.zh: 是月，薨。

translations.literal: That same month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same month.

sentences.zh: 追封親王，賞銀五千兩治喪，諡曰敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank; five thousand taels of silver were granted for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created a full prince. Five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he received the posthumous name Min.

sentences.zh: 溥煦襲郡王。

translations.literal: Puxu inherited the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Puxu succeeded to the princedom of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十三年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu he died and was given the posthumous title Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Guangxu 33 and received the posthumous name Shen.

sentences.zh: 子毓朗，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yulang inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yulang succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，授民政部侍郎、步軍統領。

translations.literal: At the end of the Guangxu reign he was appointed Vice Minister of Civil Affairs and metropolitan commandant of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangxu reign he was appointed Vice Minister of Civil Affairs and metropolitan infantry commandant.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年七月，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Xuantong he was appointed a Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xuantong 2 he was appointed to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，改授軍諮大臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he was transferred to the Military Advisory Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he was reassigned to the Military Advisory Council.

sentences.zh: 端慧太子永璉，高宗第二子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Duanhui Yonglian was Emperor Gaozong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Duanhui Yonglian was Gaozong's second son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年十月，殤，年九歲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Qianlong he died young, aged nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qianlong 3 he died in childhood at the age of nine.

sentences.zh: 十一月，諭曰：「永璉乃皇后所生，朕之嫡子，聰明貴重，氣宇不凡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict said: "Yonglian was born of the empress, my legitimate son—intelligent and noble in bearing, with an uncommon presence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor decreed: "Yonglian was born of the empress, my legitimate son—bright, noble in bearing, and possessed of an uncommon presence.

sentences.zh: 皇考命名，隱示承宗器之意。

translations.literal: My imperial father's naming of him secretly showed the intent that he should inherit the dynastic vessel.
translations.idiomatic: My father's choice of name already hinted that he was meant to inherit the throne.

sentences.zh: 朕御極後，恪守成式，親書密旨，召諸大臣藏於乾清宮「正大光明」榜後，是雖未冊立，已命為皇太子矣。

translations.literal: After I took the throne I observed the established practice, personally wrote a secret edict, summoned the great ministers, and had it stored behind the 'Upright and Glorious' plaque in the Palace of Heavenly Purity—thus, though he was not formally installed, he had already been designated crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After my accession I followed established practice, wrote a secret edict in my own hand, summoned the senior ministers, and had it placed behind the 'Upright and Glorious' plaque in the Palace of Heavenly Purity—so that although he was never formally installed, he had already been named heir.

sentences.zh: 今既薨逝，一切典禮用皇太子儀注行。」

translations.literal: Now that he has died, all rites shall follow the regulations for a crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, every ceremony shall follow the regulations prescribed for a crown prince."

sentences.zh: 旋冊贈皇太子，諡端慧。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was posthumously enfeoffed as crown prince, with the posthumous title Duanhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously created crown prince with the temple name Duanhui.

sentences.zh: 循郡王永璋，高宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Xun Yongzhang was Emperor Gaozong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xun Yongzhang was Gaozong's third son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年七月，薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Qianlong 25.

sentences.zh: 追封循郡王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以永瑆子綿懿為後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Yongrong's son Mianyi was made heir and inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year Yongrong's son Mianyi was named heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，子奕緒，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yixu inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Yixu succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子載遷，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zaiqian inherited as state-supporting duke.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Zaiqian succeeded as a state-supporting duke.

sentences.zh: 榮純親王永琪，高宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Rongchun Yongqi was Emperor Gaozong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rongchun Yongqi was Gaozong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十年十一月，封榮親王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirtieth year of Qianlong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qianlong 30 he was created Prince of Rong.

sentences.zh: 永琪少習騎射，嫺國語，上鍾愛之。

translations.literal: Yongqi from youth practiced riding and archery, was skilled in Manchu, and the emperor cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yongqi trained in riding and archery, was fluent in Manchu, and the emperor doted on him.

sentences.zh: 三十一年三月，薨，諡曰純。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-first year he died and was given the posthumous title Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the thirty-first year and received the posthumous name Chun.

sentences.zh: 子綿億，四十九年十一月，封貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Mianyi, in the eleventh month of the forty-ninth year, was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianyi was created beile in the eleventh month of the forty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年正月，襲榮郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jiaqing he inherited as Prince of Rong of the commandery rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaqing 4 he succeeded to the princedom of Rong.

sentences.zh: 綿億少孤，體羸多病，特聰敏，工書，熟經史。

translations.literal: Mianyi lost his father young, was frail and often ill, yet was exceptionally clever, skilled at calligraphy, and versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Mianyi was orphaned young, frail and often ill, yet unusually quick-witted, accomplished in calligraphy, and well versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 十八年，林清變起，綿億方扈蹕，聞警，力請上速還京師，上即日回鑾，因重視之，寵眷日渥。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Lin Qing disturbance broke out. Mianyi was then attending the imperial progress; hearing the alarm, he urgently begged the emperor to return swiftly to the capital. The emperor returned the same day and thereafter valued him, his favor growing daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Lin Qing uprising erupted, Mianyi was with the imperial procession. On hearing the alarm he urgently urged the emperor to return at once to the capital. The emperor turned back that very day and thereafter held him in high regard, his favor deepening day by day.

sentences.zh: 逾年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: The following year he died and was given the posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died and received the posthumous name Ke.

sentences.zh: 子奕繪，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yihui inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yihui succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，子載鈞，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zaijun inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Zaijun succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子溥楣，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: He died; his son Pumei inherited as state-supporting duke.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Pumei succeeded as a state-supporting duke.

sentences.zh: 哲親王永琮，高宗第七子，與端慧太子同為嫡子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhe Yongzong was Emperor Gaozong's seventh son and, like Crown Prince Duanhui, was a son of the legitimate wife.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhe Yongzong was Gaozong's seventh son and, like Crown Prince Duanhui, was born of the empress.

sentences.zh: 端慧太子薨，高宗屬意焉。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Duanhui died, Emperor Gaozong set his hopes on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Duanhui's death, Gaozong fixed his hopes on him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年十二月，以痘殤，方二歲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year of Qianlong he died of smallpox, aged only two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Qianlong 12 he died of smallpox at the age of two.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「先朝未有以元後正嫡紹承大統者，朕乃欲行先人所未行之事，邀先人不能獲之福，此乃朕過耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "In former reigns no legitimate son of the primary consort ever succeeded to the great inheritance. I wished to do what our forebears had not done and to seek a blessing our forebears could not obtain—is this my fault!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lamented: "No previous reign had ever passed the throne to the legitimate son of the primary empress. I meant to do what our ancestors had not done and to claim a blessing they could never win—is this my own fault?"

sentences.zh: 命喪儀視皇子從優，諡曰悼敏。

translations.literal: He ordered funeral rites for a prince with extra favor and gave the posthumous title Daomin.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered funeral rites for a prince on the most generous scale and gave him the posthumous name Daomin.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年三月，追封哲親王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 4 he was posthumously created Prince of Zhe.

sentences.zh: 儀慎親王永璇，高宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Yishen Yongxuan was Emperor Gaozong's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yishen Yongxuan was Gaozong's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十四年，封儀郡王。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi of the commandery rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 44 he was created Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年正月，進封親王，總理吏部。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jiaqing he was advanced to prince of the first rank and made general supervisor of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaqing 4 he was promoted to full prince and placed in general charge of the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 二月，罷。

translations.literal: In the second month he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was relieved of the post.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「六卿分職，各有專司，原無總理之名，勿啟專權之漸。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "The six ministers divide duties, each with his own charge; there was originally no title of general supervisor—do not open the way to monopolization of power."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The six ministers each have defined duties; there was never a title of general supervisor—do not open the door to concentrated power."

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，諭曰：「內廷行走諸王日入直，儀親王朕長兄，年逾六十，冬寒無事，不必進內。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year an edict said: "Princes who serve within the palace enter duty daily. Prince Yi is my elder brother, past sixty; in winter cold when there is no business, he need not enter within."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year the emperor ruled: "Princes serving in the inner court attend daily. Prince Yi is my elder brother, already past sixty; in the winter cold, when there is no pressing business, he need not come inside."

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，封其子綿志為貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year his son Mianzhi was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year his son Mianzhi was created beile.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以武英殿刻高宗聖訓，誤書廟諱，罷王俸三年。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the Hall of Martial Glory's printing of Emperor Gaozong's sacred instructions miswrote a temple taboo, his princely stipend was suspended for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, because the Hall of Martial Glory's edition of Gaozong's sacred instructions violated an imperial taboo, his princely stipend was withheld for three years.

sentences.zh: 十八年，林清變起，賊入禁城，綿志從宣宗發鳥槍殪賊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Lin Qing disturbance broke out; rebels entered the Forbidden City. Mianzhi followed the future Emperor Xuanzong in firing muskets and killing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Lin Qing uprising brought rebels into the Forbidden City, Mianzhi followed the future Emperor Xuanzong in firing muskets and killing the attackers.

sentences.zh: 仁宗褒其奮勇，加郡王銜，加俸歲千兩。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong praised his valor, granted him the rank of prince of the commandery, and added one thousand taels to his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised his courage, granted him princely rank of the commandery, and added a thousand taels to his yearly stipend.

sentences.zh: 永璇亦以督捕勤勞，免一切處分。

translations.literal: Yongxuan also, for diligent labor in supervising the pursuit, was exempted from all penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxuan, too, for his diligent work in supervising the pursuit, was spared every penalty.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，命祭裕陵，阻雨，還京，坐降郡王，並奪綿志郡王銜及加俸，仍罰王俸五年。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year he was ordered to sacrifice at the Yuling mausoleum; blocked by rain, he returned to the capital and was demoted to prince of the commandery; Mianzhi's commandery rank and added stipend were also taken away, and princely stipend was still fined for five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year he was sent to offer sacrifice at the Yuling mausoleum. Rain forced him back to the capital, and he was demoted to commandery prince; Mianzhi's princely rank and added stipend were stripped as well, and his own stipend was fined for another five years.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月，复綿志郡王銜，賜三眼孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year Mianzhi's commandery rank was restored and he was granted a three-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year Mianzhi's princely rank was restored and he was awarded a three-eyed peacock plume.

sentences.zh: 七月，坐刺探政事，上諭曰：「朕兄儀親王年已七十有四，精力漸衰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, for prying into state affairs, the emperor issued an edict saying: "My elder brother Prince Yi is already seventy-four, his vigor gradually failing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, for meddling in government affairs, the emperor decreed: "My elder brother Prince Yi is already seventy-four, and his strength is failing.

sentences.zh: 所領事務甚多，恐有貽誤，探聽尚有可原。

translations.literal: The affairs under his charge are many, and I fear mistakes; his listening in may still be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: The duties he oversees are numerous, and I fear errors; his eavesdropping may yet be excused.

sentences.zh: 朕不忍煩勞長兄，致失頤養。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to trouble my elder brother and cause him to lose his ease in old age.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to burden my elder brother and deprive him of a peaceful old age.

sentences.zh: 嗣後止留內廷行走，平日不必入直。」

translations.literal: Henceforth he is only to remain in palace service; on ordinary days he need not enter duty."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter he is to retain only his place in palace service and need not attend daily duty."

sentences.zh: 六月，綿志坐縱妾父冒職官詐贓，奪郡王銜，罰貝勒俸四年。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Mianzhi, for allowing his concubine's father to usurp an office and extort bribes, was stripped of his commandery rank and fined four years of beile stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Mianzhi was stripped of his princely rank and fined four years of beile stipend for letting his concubine's father hold office under false pretenses and extort bribes.

sentences.zh: 二十五年七月，宣宗即位，諭儀親王不必遠迎，又諭召對宴賚無庸叩拜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, when Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he ordered that Prince Yi need not go far to welcome him, and also ruled that at audiences, banquets, and gifts he need not perform the full prostration.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, when Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he excused Prince Yi from going far to welcome him and ruled that at audiences, banquets, and bestowals he need not perform the full kowtow.

sentences.zh: 道光三年正月，綿志复郡王銜，加俸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Daoguang Mianzhi's commandery rank was restored and his stipend increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daoguang 3 Mianzhi's princely rank was restored and his stipend increased.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，命在紫禁城乘轎，並加賞俸銀五千，示親親敬長之意。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he was ordered to ride in a sedan chair within the Forbidden City and was additionally granted five thousand taels of stipend silver, showing the intent to cherish kin and honor elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he was permitted to travel by sedan chair within the Forbidden City and was granted an additional five thousand taels of stipend silver, in token of affection for kin and respect for elders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，复諭朝賀免行禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict again excused him from performing rites at court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was again excused from performing ceremonial obeisance at court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 十年十月，永璇詣圓明園視大阿哥，徑入福園門，諭罷綿志官。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year Yongxuan went to the Old Summer Palace to visit the eldest imperial son, entered straight through the Fuyuan Gate, and an edict dismissed Mianzhi from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year Yongxuan went to the Old Summer Palace to visit the eldest imperial son, entered directly through the Fuyuan Gate, and Mianzhi was dismissed from office by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諭壽皇殿、安佑宮當行禮時，於府第內行禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ruled that when rites were due at the Hall of Imperial Longevity and the Palace of Ancestral Blessing, he should perform them within his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to perform rites owed at the Hall of Imperial Longevity and the Palace of Ancestral Blessing within his own residence.

sentences.zh: 又諭元旦暨正月十四日宗親筵宴，均免其入宴，別頒果殽一席。

translations.literal: It was further ruled that at the New Year's Day and fourteenth-day-of-the-first-month banquets for imperial kin he was excused from attending and was separately granted one tray of fruit and delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: He was also excused from the New Year's and fourteenth-of-the-first-month banquets for imperial kin and was instead sent a separate tray of fruit and delicacies.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，薨，年八十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the twelfth year at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 賜銀五千治喪，親臨賜奠，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: Five thousand taels of silver were granted for the funeral; the emperor came in person to bestow offerings, and he was given the posthumous title Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral. The emperor came in person to offer libations, and he received the posthumous name Shen.

sentences.zh: 綿志襲郡王，薨，諡曰順。

translations.literal: Mianzhi inherited as prince of the commandery; he died and was given the posthumous title Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhi succeeded to the princedom; when he died he received the posthumous name Shun.

sentences.zh: 子奕絪，襲貝勒，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: His son Yishen inherited as beile and was given the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yishen succeeded as beile and was granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，曾孫毓崐，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He died; his great-grandson Yukun inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his great-grandson Yukun succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟毓岐，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: He died; his younger brother Yuqi inherited as state-supporting duke.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his younger brother Yuqi succeeded as a state-supporting duke.

sentences.zh: 成哲親王永瑆，高宗第十一子。

translations.literal: Prince Chengzhe Yongrong was Emperor Gaozong's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengzhe Yongrong was Gaozong's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年，封成親王。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he was created Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 永瑆幼工書，高宗愛之，每幸其府第。

translations.literal: From youth Yongrong was skilled at calligraphy; Emperor Gaozong loved him and often visited his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yongrong showed early mastery of calligraphy, and Gaozong doted on him, often visiting his residence.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年正月，仁宗命在軍機處行走，總理戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jiaqing Emperor Renzong ordered him to serve in the Grand Council and take general charge of the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaqing 4 Emperor Renzong placed him on the Grand Council and in general charge of the Board of Revenue's three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 故事，親王無領軍機者，領軍機自永瑆始。

translations.literal: By precedent no prince had headed the Grand Council; Yongrong was the first to do so.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent no prince had headed the Grand Council; Yongrong was the first.

sentences.zh: 二月，儀親王永璇罷總理吏部，並命永瑆俟軍務奏銷事畢，不必總理戶部。

translations.literal: In the second month Prince Yi Yongxuan was dismissed from general supervision of the Board of Civil Office, and Yongrong was ordered that when military accounts were settled he need not supervise the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Prince Yi Yongxuan was relieved of general supervision of the Board of Civil Office, and Yongrong was told that once military accounts were closed he need no longer oversee the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三月，和珅以罪誅，沒其園第，賜永瑆。

translations.literal: In the third month Heshen was executed for his crimes and his garden residence confiscated and granted to Yongrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Heshen was executed for his crimes; his garden mansion was confiscated and given to Yongrong.

sentences.zh: 七月，永瑆辭總理戶部三庫，允之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yongrong resigned general supervision of the three treasuries; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yongrong resigned supervision of the three treasuries, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 八月，編修洪亮吉上書永瑆，譏切朝政，永瑆上聞，上治亮吉罪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the compiler Hong Liangji sent Yongrong a letter sharply criticizing court governance; Yongrong reported it, and the emperor punished Liangji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the compiler Hong Liangji wrote Yongrong a letter sharply criticizing the government. Yongrong reported it, and the emperor punished Liangji.

sentences.zh: 語在亮吉傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Liangji's biography.
translations.idiomatic: This is recounted in Liangji's biography.

sentences.zh: 十月，上諭曰：「自設軍機處，無諸王行走。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the emperor issued an edict saying: "Since the Grand Council was established, no prince has served there.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor decreed: "Since the Grand Council was established, no prince has served on it.

sentences.zh: 因軍務較繁，暫令永瑆入直，究與國家定制未符。

translations.literal: Because military affairs were unusually heavy, Yongrong was temporarily ordered to enter duty, but this ultimately did not accord with the state's established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Because military affairs were unusually pressing, Yongrong was temporarily placed on duty, but this did not accord with established state practice.

sentences.zh: 罷軍機處行走。」

translations.literal: He was dismissed from service in the Grand Council."
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from the Grand Council."

sentences.zh: 永瑆嘗聞康熙中內監言其師少時及見董其昌以前三指握管懸腕作書，永瑆廣其說，作撥鐙法，推論書旨，深得古人用筆之意。

translations.literal: Yongrong once heard a palace eunuch of the Kangxi era say that his teacher in youth had seen Dong Qichang write with three fingers gripping the brush and the wrist suspended; Yongrong expanded on this, devised the lamp-pushing method, and in expounding the aim of calligraphy deeply grasped the ancients' intent in wielding the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Yongrong once heard a Kangxi-era palace eunuch say that his teacher in youth had seen Dong Qichang write with three fingers on the brush and the wrist lifted from the table. Yongrong developed this into his lamp-pushing method and, in expounding the principles of calligraphy, captured the ancients' understanding of the brush.

sentences.zh: 上命書裕陵聖德神功碑，並令自擇書跡刻為詒晉齋帖，以手詔為序。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to write the Stele of Sagely Virtue and Divine Merit at the Yuling mausoleum and to select his own calligraphy to be carved as the Yijin Studio modelbook, with an autograph preface.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to inscribe the Stele of Sagely Virtue and Divine Merit at the Yuling mausoleum and to choose his own calligraphic works for carving as the Yijin Studio modelbook, with an autograph preface.

sentences.zh: 刻成，頒賞臣工。

translations.literal: When carving was complete, it was distributed and bestowed on officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the carving was finished, copies were distributed to officials.

sentences.zh: 十八年，林清變起，永瑆在紫禁城內督捕，上嘉其勤勞，免一切處分及未完罰俸。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Lin Qing disturbance broke out, Yongrong supervised the pursuit within the Forbidden City; the emperor praised his diligence and exempted him from all penalties and unpaid fined stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, during the Lin Qing uprising, Yongrong supervised the pursuit inside the Forbidden City. The emperor praised his diligence and remitted every penalty and unpaid stipend fine.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月，加其子不入八分輔國公綿懃郡王銜。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year his son, the buluo-fen auxiliary state duke Mianqin, was given the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year his son Mianqin, an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges, was granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 五月，祭地壇，終獻時，贊引誤，永瑆依以行禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, at sacrifice at the Altar of Earth, during the final offering the invocator erred and Yongrong followed him in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, at the sacrifice at the Altar of Earth, the invocator made an error during the final offering and Yongrong followed his mistaken lead.

sentences.zh: 上以永瑆年老多病，罷一切差使，不必在內廷行走，於邸第閉門思過，罰親王半俸十年。

translations.literal: Because Yongrong was old and often ill, the emperor dismissed him from all assignments, ordered that he need not serve in the inner court, had him shut his gates at his mansion to reflect on his faults, and fined half his princely stipend for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yongrong was old and often ill, the emperor relieved him of every assignment, excused him from inner-court service, ordered him to remain at his mansion in penitential seclusion, and fined half his princely stipend for ten years.

sentences.zh: 綿懃亦罷內大臣，居家侍父。

translations.literal: Mianqin was also dismissed as inner minister and remained at home to attend his father.
translations.idiomatic: Mianqin was also dismissed as inner minister and stayed home to attend his father.

sentences.zh: 二十五年六月，綿懃卒，贈郡王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year Mianqin died and was posthumously granted the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year Mianqin died and was posthumously created a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 有司請諡，以非例斥之，著為令。

translations.literal: The authorities requested a posthumous title; it was rejected as not according to precedent and made a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities requested a posthumous title, but it was rejected as irregular and the refusal was made a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，有旨免迎謁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong died, an edict excused him from going out to welcome and pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong died, an edict excused him from going out to welcome the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 語見儀親王傳。

translations.literal: The account appears in the biography of Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: This is recorded in the biography of Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 十月，命曾孫載銳襲貝勒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month his great-grandson Zairui was ordered to inherit as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month his great-grandson Zairui was ordered to succeed as beile.

sentences.zh: 道光二年十月，上還自行在，永瑆進食品十六器，以非例卻之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Daoguang, when the emperor returned from the traveling palace, Yongrong presented sixteen vessels of food; it was refused as irregular.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Daoguang 2, when the emperor returned from the traveling palace, Yongrong presented sixteen dishes of food, but the gift was refused as irregular.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，薨，年七十二，賜銀五千治喪，諡曰哲。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he died, aged seventy-two; five thousand taels of silver were granted for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the third year at seventy-two. Five thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he received the posthumous name Zhe.

sentences.zh: 載銳襲郡王。

translations.literal: Zairui inherited as prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zairui succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 綿懃及載銳父奕綬並追封如其爵。

translations.literal: Mianqin and Zairui's father Yishou were both posthumously enfeoffed according to their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Mianqin and Zairui's father Yishou were both posthumously created to ranks matching their titles.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he died and was given the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianfeng 9 and received the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子溥莊，襲貝勒，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: His son Puzhuang inherited as beile and was given the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puzhuang succeeded as beile and was granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，子毓橚，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He died; his son Yushu inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his son Yushu succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 貝勒永璂，高宗第十二子。

translations.literal: Beile Yongji was Emperor Gaozong's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Yongji was Gaozong's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 41.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年三月，追封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jiaqing 4 he was posthumously created beile.

sentences.zh: 以成親王子綿偲為後，初封鎮國將軍，再進封貝子。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng's son Miansi was made heir; he was first enfeoffed as state-supporting general and twice advanced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng's son Miansi was named heir; he was first created a state-supporting general and later promoted twice to beizi.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年正月，諭曰：「綿偲逮事皇祖，昔同朕在上書房讀書者只綿偲一人。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year of Daoguang an edict said: "Miansi served our imperial grandfather; of those who once studied with me in the Upper Study Hall, Miansi alone remains."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daoguang 18 the emperor said: "Miansi served my grandfather; of those who once studied with me in the Upper Study Hall, only Miansi remains."

sentences.zh: 進貝勒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，子奕縉，襲貝子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; his son Yijin inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year; his son Yijin succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟奕繕，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: He died; his younger brother Yishan inherited as state-supporting duke.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his younger brother Yishan succeeded as a state-supporting duke.

sentences.zh: 慶僖親王永璘，高宗第十七子。

translations.literal: Prince Qingxi Yonglin was Emperor Gaozong's seventeenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qingxi Yonglin was Gaozong's seventeenth son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he was created beile.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年正月，仁宗親政，封惠郡王，尋改封慶郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jiaqing, when Emperor Renzong assumed personal rule, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hui of the commandery rank and soon after as Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiaqing 4, when Emperor Renzong assumed personal rule, he was created Prince of Hui and soon after Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 三月，和珅誅，沒其宅賜永璘。

translations.literal: In the third month Heshen was executed and his residence confiscated and granted to Yonglin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Heshen was executed; his residence was confiscated and given to Yonglin.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，以祝穎貴太妃七十壽未奏明，命退出乾清門，留內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, because he had not reported in advance the seventieth birthday of Imperial Noble Consort Zhu Yinggui, he was ordered to withdraw from the Gate of Heavenly Purity but to remain in inner-court service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, because he had not reported in advance the seventieth birthday of Imperial Noble Consort Zhu Yinggui, he was ordered to withdraw from the Gate of Heavenly Purity while retaining inner-court duties.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月朔，乾清宮筵宴，輔國公綿？

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the twenty-first year, at a banquet in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, the auxiliary state duke Mianmin
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the twenty-first year, at a banquet in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, the auxiliary state duke Mianmin

sentences.zh: 就席遲，奕紹推令入座，拂墮食，

translations.literal: was late taking his seat; Yishao pushed him to sit down and knocked over food bowls.
translations.idiomatic: was late taking his seat; Yishao pushed him to sit down and knocked over the food bowls.

sentences.zh: 永璘告內奏事太監。

translations.literal: Yonglin reported this to the inner memorializing eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglin reported the matter to the inner memorializing eunuch.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「諸王奏事不得迳交內奏事太監。」

translations.literal: An edict was received: "Princes memorializing affairs must not hand them directly to the inner memorializing eunuch."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "When princes report affairs they must not hand memorials directly to the inner memorializing eunuch."

sentences.zh: 罰永璘俸。

translations.literal: Yonglin's stipend was fined.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglin's stipend was fined.

sentences.zh: 二十五年三月，永璘疾篤，上親臨視，命進封親王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year Yonglin was gravely ill; the emperor came in person to visit and ordered that he be advanced to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-fifth year Yonglin fell gravely ill. The emperor visited him in person and ordered that he be promoted to full prince.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died and was given the posthumous title Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and received the posthumous name Xi.

sentences.zh: 命皇子往奠，上時謁陵歸，复親臨焉。

translations.literal: Princes were ordered to go and offer libations; when the emperor returned from visiting the mausoleum he again came in person.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were ordered to offer libations; when the emperor returned from visiting the imperial tombs he came in person as well.

sentences.zh: 子綿慜，襲郡王。

translations.literal: His son Mianmin inherited as prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianmin succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 綿慜奏府中有毘盧帽門口四座、太平缸五十四件、銅路鐙三十六對。

translations.literal: Mianmin reported that in the mansion there were four Vairocana-cap gateways, fifty-four great peace jars, and thirty-six pairs of bronze road lamps.
translations.idiomatic: Mianmin reported that his mansion held four gateways with Vairocana caps, fifty-four great peace jars, and thirty-six pairs of bronze road lamps.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「慶親王府第本為和珅舊宅，凡此違制之物，皆和珅私置。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "The mansion of the Prince of Qing was originally Heshen's old residence; all these objects in violation of regulations were privately installed by Heshen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "The Prince of Qing's mansion was once Heshen's residence; all these objects that violate regulations were Heshen's private additions.

sentences.zh: 嗣後王、貝勒、貝子當依會典，服物寧失之不及，不可僭逾，庶幾永保令名。」

translations.literal: Hereafter princes, beile, and beizi should follow the Collected Statutes; in dress and objects it is better to fall short than to overstep, so that they may long preserve a good name."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth princes, beile, and beizi must follow the Collected Statutes: in dress and furnishings it is better to fall short than to overstep, if they wish to preserve a good name."

sentences.zh: 府置諳達二，亦命裁汰。

translations.literal: Two Manchu-language instructors maintained at the mansion were also ordered cut.
translations.idiomatic: The two Manchu instructors kept at the mansion were also ordered dismissed.

sentences.zh: 道光三年正月，賜綿慜三眼孔雀翎，管雍和宮、中正殿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Daoguang Mianmin was granted a three-eyed peacock feather and put in charge of the Yonghe Temple and the Zhongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daoguang 3 Mianmin was awarded a three-eyed peacock plume and placed in charge of the Yonghe Temple and the Zhongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，薨，賜銀四千治喪，諡曰良。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year he died; four thousand taels of silver were granted for the funeral, and he was given the posthumous title Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the sixteenth year. Four thousand taels of silver were granted for his funeral, and he received the posthumous name Liang.

sentences.zh: 上命再襲郡王一次。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that the commandery princedom be inherited one more time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the princedom be inherited one further generation at commandery rank.

sentences.zh: 以儀順郡王綿志子奕採為後，襲郡王。

translations.literal: Prince Yishun Mianzhi's son Yicai was made heir and inherited as prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhi's son Yicai of the Prince Yishun line was named heir and succeeded to the princedom.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，命在御前行走。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to attend before the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十二年十月，奕採以服中納妾，下宗人府議處。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year Yicai took a concubine while in mourning; the case was sent to the Imperial Clan Court for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year Yicai took a concubine during mourning; the Imperial Clan Court was ordered to deliberate his punishment.

sentences.zh: 奕採行賕請免，永璘第六子輔國公綿性亦行賕覬襲王爵，事發，奕採奪爵，綿性戍盛京。

translations.literal: Yicai offered bribes to seek exemption; Yonglin's sixth son, the auxiliary state duke Mianxing, also bribed in hope of inheriting the princedom. When the affair came to light, Yicai was stripped of his title and Mianxing was banished to Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Yicai offered bribes to escape punishment; Yonglin's sixth son Mianxing, an auxiliary state duke, also bribed in hope of inheriting the princedom. When the affair was exposed, Yicai was stripped of his title and Mianxing was exiled to Mukden.

sentences.zh: 以永璘第五子不入八分鎮國公綿悌奉永璘祀。

translations.literal: Yonglin's fifth son, the buluo-fen state-supporting duke Mianti, was appointed to maintain Yonglin's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglin's fifth son Mianti, a state-supporting duke outside the Eight Privileges, was appointed to maintain Yonglin's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 旋又坐​​事，降鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was again convicted of an offense and demoted to state-supporting general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was convicted of another offense and demoted to state-supporting general.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 以綿性子奕劻為後。

translations.literal: Mianxing's son Yikuang was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Mianxing's son Yikuang was named heir.

sentences.zh: 三十年，襲輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he inherited as auxiliary state general.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he succeeded as auxiliary state general.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年正月，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xianfeng he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xianfeng 2 he was created beizi.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，上三十萬壽，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, on the emperor's thirtieth birthday, he was advanced to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, on the emperor's thirtieth birthday, he was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年九月，大婚，加郡王銜，授御前大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year of Tongzhi, at the grand wedding, he was given the rank of prince of the commandery and appointed an imperial presence minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Tongzhi 11, at the grand wedding, he was granted princely rank of the commandery and appointed minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年三月，命管理總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Guangxu he was ordered to manage the Yamen for the General Management of Affairs of All Nations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangxu 10 he was ordered to head the Yamen for the General Management of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十月，進慶郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was advanced to Prince of Qing of the commandery rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，會同醇親王辦理海軍事務。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he was jointly charged with Prince Chun to manage naval affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he was jointly assigned with Prince Chun to manage naval affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，命在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he was ordered to serve within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year he was ordered to serve in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，授右宗正。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he was appointed right director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he was appointed right director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 大婚，賜四團正龍補服，子載振頭品頂帶。

translations.literal: At the grand wedding he was granted a four-round-dragon supplementary robe, and his son Zaizhen was given a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand wedding he was granted a four-round-dragon supplementary robe, and his son Zaizhen was given a first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 二十年，太后六十萬壽，懿旨進親王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, on the empress dowager's sixtieth birthday, an edict of grace advanced him to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, on the empress dowager's sixtieth birthday, a gracious edict promoted him to full prince.

sentences.zh: 二十六年七月，上奉太后幸太原，命奕劻留京會大學士李鴻章與各國議和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year the emperor escorted the empress dowager to Taiyuan and ordered Yikuang to remain in the capital to join Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang in negotiating peace with the various powers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-sixth year the emperor escorted the empress dowager to Taiyuan and left Yikuang in the capital to join Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang in peace negotiations with the foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 二十七年六月，改總理各國事務衙門為外務部，奕劻仍總理部事。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year the Yamen for General Management of Affairs of All Nations was changed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Yikuang continued as its general supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-seventh year the Yamen for Foreign Affairs was reorganized as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Yikuang remained at its head.

sentences.zh: 十二月，加載振貝子銜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zaizhen was given the rank of beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zaizhen was granted the rank of beizi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年三月，授奕劻軍機大臣，仍總理外務部如故。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year Yikuang was appointed a Grand Councilor while continuing as before to supervise the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year Yikuang was appointed to the Grand Council while continuing to head the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋命總理財政處、練兵處，解御前大臣以授載振。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to supervise the Bureau of Finance and the Office of Army Training, and was relieved of the post of imperial presence minister, which was granted to Zaizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was placed in charge of the Bureau of Finance and the Office of Army Training, and his post as minister in attendance was transferred to Zaizhen.

sentences.zh: 載振赴日本大阪觀展覽會歸，請振興商務，設商部，即以載振為尚書。

translations.literal: When Zaizhen returned from viewing the exhibition in Osaka, Japan, he requested promotion of commerce, the establishment of a Ministry of Commerce, and Zaizhen was appointed its minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Zaizhen returned from viewing the exhibition in Osaka, he proposed reviving commerce and creating a Ministry of Commerce, and Zaizhen was appointed its minister.

sentences.zh: 十月，御史張元奇劾載振宴集召歌妓侑酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the censor Zhang Yuanqi impeached Zaizhen for holding banquets and summoning singing girls to ply the wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Censor Zhang Yuanqi impeached Zaizhen for holding banquets with singing girls to entertain his guests.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「當深加警惕，有則改之，無則加勉。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "You must be deeply on your guard; where there is fault, correct it; where there is none, strive all the harder."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admonished him: "Be doubly vigilant—correct what is wrong, and where nothing is wrong, strive all the harder still."

sentences.zh: 旋請開缺，未許。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he requested to vacate his post; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to resign his office, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 三十年三月，御史蔣式瑆奏：「戶部設立銀行，招商入股。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirtieth year Censor Jiang Shixing memorialized: "The Ministry of Revenue is establishing a bank and inviting merchants to purchase shares.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirtieth year Censor Jiang Shixing submitted a memorial: "The Ministry of Revenue has established a bank and is inviting merchants to buy shares.

sentences.zh: 臣風聞上年十一月慶親王奕劻將私產一百二十萬送往東交民巷英商匯豐銀行收存。

translations.literal: I have heard on good authority that in the eleventh month of last year Prince Qing Yikuang deposited 1.2 million taels of his private property for safekeeping at the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, a British merchant bank in the Legation Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that last November Prince Qing Yikuang deposited 1.2 million taels of personal wealth at the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank in the Legation Quarter.

sentences.zh: 奕劻自簡任軍機大臣以來，細大不捐，門庭如市。

translations.literal: Since Yikuang's selection as Grand Councilor, nothing great or small has been refused, and his gate is like a marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yikuang's appointment to the Grand Council, he has turned away nothing great or small—his gate has been thronged like a marketplace.

sentences.zh: 是以其父子起居、飲食、車馬、衣服異常揮霍，尚能儲蓄鉅款。

translations.literal: Thus father and son maintain an extravagantly lavish way of life in lodging, food, carriage, and clothing, yet still amass great sums.
translations.idiomatic: Yet despite the extraordinary extravagance of father and son in every aspect of daily life, they have still managed to accumulate a vast fortune.

sentences.zh: 請命將此款提交官立銀行入股。」

translations.literal: I request that this sum be ordered submitted as shares in the government bank."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be ordered to invest this sum in the government bank."

sentences.zh: 命左都御史清銳、戶部尚書鹿傳霖按其事，不得實，式瑆回原衙門行走。

translations.literal: The left censor-in-chief Qing Rui and Minister of Revenue Lu Chuanlin were ordered to investigate; no proof was found, and Shixing returned to his original yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Qing Rui and Minister of Revenue Lu Chuanlin were ordered to investigate. They found no proof, and Shixing returned to his original post.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，充日、俄修訂東三省條約全權大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he served as plenipotentiary for revising the treaty on the Three Eastern Provinces with Japan and Russia.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was appointed plenipotentiary commissioner for revising the treaty on the Three Eastern Provinces with Japan and Russia.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，遣載振使奉天、吉林按事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Zaizhen was dispatched to investigate affairs in Fengtian and Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year Zaizhen was sent to Fengtian and Jilin on an investigative mission.

sentences.zh: 改商部為農工商部，仍以載振為尚書。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Commerce was changed to the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce, and Zaizhen remained its minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Commerce was reorganized as the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce, and Zaizhen remained at its head.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，命奕劻兼管陸軍部事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Yikuang was ordered to manage concurrently the affairs of the Army Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year Yikuang was placed in charge of the Army Ministry as well.

sentences.zh: 東三省改設督撫，以直隸候補道段芝貴署黑龍江巡撫。

translations.literal: Governors-general and governors were established in the Three Eastern Provinces; Duan Zhigui, an expectant intendant of Zhili, was made acting governor of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Eastern Provinces were given governors-general and governors; Duan Zhigui, an expectant intendant of Zhili, was appointed acting governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啟霖奏：「段芝貴善於迎合，上年貝子載振往東三省，道經天津，芝貴以萬二千金鬻歌妓以獻，又以十萬金為奕劻壽，夤緣得官。」

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin memorialized: "Duan Zhigui is skilled at currying favor. Last year when Beizi Zaizhen traveled to the Three Eastern Provinces via Tianjin, Zhigui sold a singing girl for twelve thousand taels as a gift, and gave one hundred thousand taels for Yikuang's birthday; by such connections he obtained office."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Qilin memorialized: "Duan Zhigui excels at ingratiation. Last year, when Beizi Zaizhen traveled through Tianjin en route to the Three Eastern Provinces, Zhigui procured a singing girl for twelve thousand taels as a gift and donated one hundred thousand taels toward Yikuang's birthday—buying his way into office."

sentences.zh: 上為罷芝貴，而命醇親王載灃、大學士孫家鼐按其事，不得實，奪啟霖官。

translations.literal: The emperor removed Zhigui from office, but ordered Prince Chun Zaifeng and Grand Secretary Sun Jia'nai to investigate; no proof was found, and Qilin was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Zhigui and ordered Prince Chun Zaifeng and Grand Secretary Sun Jia'nai to investigate. Finding no proof, they stripped Qilin of his office.

sentences.zh: 載振复疏辭御前大臣、農工商部尚書，許之。

translations.literal: Zaizhen again memorialized to resign as imperial presence minister and minister of the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zaizhen again submitted his resignation from his posts as minister in attendance and head of the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce, and was permitted to step down.

sentences.zh: 三十四年十一月，命以親王世襲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirty-fourth year princely rank was ordered to pass by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the thirty-fourth year he was granted princedom with perpetual hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年四月，罷軍機處，授奕劻內閣總理大臣，大學士那桐、徐世昌協理大臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Xuantong the Grand Council was abolished; Yikuang was appointed premier of the cabinet, with grand secretaries Natong and Xu Shichang as associate premiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xuantong 3 the Grand Council was abolished. Yikuang was appointed premier of the cabinet, with Grand Secretaries Natong and Xu Shichang as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 八月，武昌兵起，初命陸軍部尚書廕昌視師，奕劻請於朝，起袁世凱湖廣總督視師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the soldiers at Wuchang rose; Yin Chang, minister of the Army, was first ordered to take command, but Yikuang requested at court that Yuan Shikai, governor-general of Huguang, be recalled to take command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Wuchang garrison mutinied. Army Minister Yin Chang was first ordered to take the field, but Yikuang urged at court that Yuan Shikai, governor-general of Huguang, be recalled to command the campaign.

sentences.zh: 世凱入京師，代奕劻為內閣總理大臣，授奕劻弼德院總裁。

translations.literal: Shikai entered the capital, replaced Yikuang as premier of the cabinet, and Yikuang was appointed president of the Academy of Moral Cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shikai came to the capital, replaced Yikuang as premier, and Yikuang was named president of the Academy of Moral Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔遜位，奕劻避居天津。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict ordered abdication; Yikuang retired to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the abdication edict was issued, and Yikuang withdrew to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 後七年薨，諡曰密。

translations.literal: Seven years later he died; he was given the posthumous title Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He died seven years later and received the posthumous name Mi.

sentences.zh: 仁宗五子：孝淑睿皇后生宣宗，孝和睿皇后生惇恪親王綿愷、瑞懷親王綿忻，恭順皇貴妃鈕祜祿氏生惠端親王綿愉，和裕皇貴妃劉氏生穆郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong had five sons: Empress Xiaoshu Rui bore the future Emperor Xuanzong; Empress Xiaohe Rui bore Prince Dunke Miankai and Prince Ruihuai Mianxin; Imperial Noble Consort Gongshun of the Niuhuru clan bore Prince Huiduan Mianyu; Imperial Noble Consort Heyu of the Liu clan bore the Prince of Mu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had five sons. Empress Xiaoshu Rui bore the future Emperor Xuanzong. Empress Xiaohe Rui bore Prince Dunke Miankai and Prince Ruihuai Mianxin. Imperial Noble Consort Gongshun of the Niuhuru clan bore Prince Huiduan Mianyu. Imperial Noble Consort Heyu of the Liu clan bore the Prince of Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆郡王，未命名，仁宗第一子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Mu commandery was unnamed; he was Emperor Renzong's first son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Mu was never given a personal name; he was Renzong's first son.

sentences.zh: 二歲，殤。

translations.literal: At age two he died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at the age of two.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，追封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong succeeded to the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 惇恪親王綿愷，仁宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Dunke Miankai was Emperor Renzong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dunke Miankai was Renzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，林清變起，綿愷隨宣宗捕賊蒼震門，得旨褒嘉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing, when the Lin Qing uprising erupted, Miankai followed the future Emperor Xuanzong in capturing bandits at Cangzhen Gate and received an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 18, when the Lin Qing uprising broke out, Miankai joined the future Xuanzong in hunting down the rebels at Cangzhen Gate and was commended by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，封惇郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Dun of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was created Prince Dun of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，進親王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was advanced to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong succeeded to the throne, Miankai was promoted to full prince.

sentences.zh: 子奕纘，封不入八分公。

translations.literal: His son Yizuan was enfeoffed as a duke outside the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yizuan was created a state duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 道光三年正月，命綿愷內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Daoguang Miankai was ordered to serve within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daoguang 3 Miankai was ordered to serve in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 旋以福晉乘轎徑入神武門，坐罷，罰王俸五年。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, because his princess consort took a sedan chair directly through the Shenwu Gate, he was dismissed from office and fined five years of princely stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his consort's sedan chair entered directly through the Shenwu Gate; he was dismissed from office and fined five years of princely stipend.

sentences.zh: 上奉太后幸綿愷第，仍命內廷行走，減罰王俸三年。

translations.literal: The emperor, escorting the empress dowager, visited Miankai's residence and again ordered him to serve in the inner court, reducing the fine to three years of stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor escorted the empress dowager to Miankai's residence, restored him to inner-court service, and reduced the stipend fine to three years.

sentences.zh: 七年，坐太監張明得私相往來，复匿太監苑長青，降郡王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for private dealings with the eunuch Zhang Mingde and for again concealing the eunuch Yuan Changqing, he was demoted to prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was demoted to commandery prince for private dealings with Eunuch Zhang Mingde and for again concealing Eunuch Yuan Changqing.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，追？

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year his past service was recounted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year his earlier service was formally acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 蒼震門捕賊，急難禦侮，复親王，諭加意檢束。

translations.literal: For capturing bandits at Cangzhen Gate and repelling danger in time of peril, he was restored to prince of the first rank, with an instruction to restrain himself carefully.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in capturing the rebels at Cangzhen Gate and standing firm against sudden danger, he was restored to full princely rank, with orders to govern himself more carefully.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，綿愷以議皇后喪禮引書「百姓如喪考妣，四海遏密八音」，於義未協，退出內廷，罰王俸十年。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year Miankai, in debating the empress's mourning rites, cited the passage "the people were as if mourning father and mother, and throughout the four seas music was hushed for eight kinds of instruments"; finding this inappropriate in meaning, he withdrew from the inner court and was fined ten years of stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year, while debating the empress's funeral rites, Miankai cited the line that "the people mourned as for a father and mother, and throughout the realm all music ceased for eight days of ritual silence." The citation was deemed improper; he withdrew from inner-court service and was fined ten years of princely stipend.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月，民婦穆氏訴其夫穆齊賢為綿愷所囚，命定郡王載銓按實，复降郡王，罷一切職任。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year the commoner woman Lady Mu complained that her husband Mu Qixian had been imprisoned by Miankai; Prince Ding of the commandery Zaiquan was ordered to investigate; the charge was substantiated; Miankai was again demoted to commandery prince and dismissed from all posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year a commoner named Lady Mu accused Miankai of imprisoning her husband Mu Qixian. Prince Ding Zaiquan was ordered to investigate; the charge was upheld. Miankai was again demoted to commandery prince and stripped of every office.

sentences.zh: 十二月，薨，复親王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; his princely rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month, and his full princely rank was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 上親臨奠，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to offer sacrifice; he was given the posthumous title Ke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended the funeral in person. Miankai received the posthumous name Ke.

sentences.zh: 奕纘前卒，追封貝勒，命賜福晉郡王半俸。

translations.literal: Yizuan had died earlier; he was posthumously created beile, and the princess consort was ordered granted half the stipend of a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yizuan had died earlier and was posthumously created beile; his consort was granted half a commandery prince's stipend.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，以皇五子奕脤為綿愷後，襲郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor's fifth son Yicong was made Miankai's heir and inherited as prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor's fifth son Yicong was named Miankai's heir and succeeded to the commandery princedom.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，命在內廷行走。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Yicong was ordered to serve in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianfeng succeeded to the throne, Yicong was ordered to serve in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 奕脤屢以失禮獲譴。

translations.literal: Yicong was repeatedly reprimanded for breaches of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yicong was repeatedly censured for lapses in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年三月，降貝勒，罷一切職任，上書房讀書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Xianfeng he was demoted to beile, dismissed from all posts, and ordered to study in the Upper Study Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xianfeng 5 he was demoted to beile, stripped of all offices, and sent to study in the Upper Study Hall.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，复封惇郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he was again enfeoffed as Prince Dun of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he was restored to the princedom of Prince Dun.

sentences.zh: 十月，進親王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was advanced to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to full prince.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，諭免叩拜稱名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, an edict exempted him from kneeling and from speaking his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi succeeded to the throne, he was exempted from kneeling in obeisance and from speaking his personal name at audience.
