sentences.zh: 同治三年，江寧克復，封其子載濂不入八分鎮國公，載津賜頭品頂帶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, when Jiangning was recovered, his son Zailian was enfeoffed as a state-supporting duke outside the Eight Privileges, and Zaijin was granted a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3, after the recapture of Jiangning, his son Zailian was created a state-supporting duke outside the Eight Privileges and Zaijin was granted a first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，授宗令。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year he was appointed director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year he was appointed imperial clan director.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，捻匪逼近畿，奕脤陳防守之策。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, as Nian bandits approached the capital region, Yicong set forth plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, as Nian rebels pressed toward the capital region, Yicong proposed defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，醇郡王奕枻劾王自授宗令，藉整頓之名，啟攬權之漸，詔兩解之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year Prince Chun of the commandery Yihuan impeached the prince for having himself appointed clan director and, under the name of rectification, opening the way toward usurping authority; an edict dismissed both from their posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year Prince Chun Yihuan impeached Yicong for securing the clan directorship for himself and, under the banner of reform, laying the groundwork for power-grabbing. An edict removed them both from office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大婚，賜紫內大臣班及帶豹尾槍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at the grand wedding, he was granted placement in the purple-rank inner ministers' roster and the right to carry a leopard-tail musket.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand wedding in the eleventh year he was granted a place among the inner ministers of purple rank and the privilege of carrying a leopard-tail musket.

sentences.zh: 載濂進輔國公。

translations.literal: Zailian was advanced to auxiliary state duke.
translations.idiomatic: Zailian was promoted to auxiliary state duke.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月，賜親？

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he was granted a prince's double stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he was granted the double stipend of a prince.

sentences.zh: 禁城乘四人肩輿，並免進領侍王雙俸。

translations.literal: He was permitted to ride a four-bearer shoulder sedan within the Forbidden City, and was also granted membership in the roster of leading bodyguard inner ministers, with exemption from advancing in obeisance at audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted a four-bearer sedan chair within the Forbidden City and granted a place among the leading bodyguard inner ministers, with exemption from advancing in obeisance at audience.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年六月，普祥峪吉地工竣，复賜食雙俸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Guangxu, when work on the auspicious site at Puxiangyu was completed, he was again granted a double stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangxu 5, after the imperial tomb site at Puxiangyu was completed, his double stipend was restored.

sentences.zh: 十三年，上親政，免帶領引見。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the emperor assumed personal rule, Yicong was exempted from leading audiences for appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when the emperor took the reins of government, Yicong was exempted from leading appointment audiences.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，薨，上奉太后臨奠，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he died; the emperor, escorting the empress dowager, attended the funeral sacrifice; he was given the posthumous title Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fifteenth year. The emperor, escorting the empress dowager, attended his funeral and granted him the posthumous name Qin.

sentences.zh: 子八，有爵者五：載濂、載漪、載瀾、載瀛、載津。

translations.literal: He had eight sons; five held titles: Zailian, Zaiyi, Zailan, Zaiying, and Zaijin.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons, five of whom held noble ranks: Zailian, Zaiyi, Zailan, Zaiying, and Zaijin.

sentences.zh: 載濂，奕脤第一子。

translations.literal: Zailian was Yicong's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Zailian was Yicong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初封一等輔國將軍，累進輔國公，襲貝勒，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as a first-rank auxiliary state general, was promoted cumulatively to auxiliary state duke, inherited as beile, and given princely rank of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Initially created a first-rank auxiliary state general, he rose through the ranks to auxiliary state duke, succeeded as beile, and was granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，子溥偁，賜頭品頂帶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year his son Pucheng was granted a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year his son Pucheng was granted a first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，載濂以庇義和拳，奪爵，弟載瀛，襲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Zailian was stripped of his title for shielding the Boxers; his brother Zaiying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Zailian was stripped of his title for protecting the Boxers, and his brother Zaiying succeeded in his place.

sentences.zh: 載瀛，奕脤第四子。

translations.literal: Zaiying was Yicong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiying was Yicong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封二等鎮國將軍，加不入八分輔國公銜，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as a second-rank state-supporting general, given the rank of auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges, and inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: Initially created a second-rank state-supporting general with the rank of an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges, he succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 載漪，奕脤第二子。

translations.literal: Zaiyi was Yicong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi was Yicong's second son.

sentences.zh: 出為瑞郡王奕志後。

translations.literal: He was given out as heir to Prince Rui of the commandery Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was adopted as heir to Prince Rui Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 獲罪，奪爵，歸宗。

translations.literal: He was convicted of an offense, stripped of his title, and returned to his original clan line.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of an offense, he was stripped of his title and restored to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 語在瑞懷親王綿忻傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biography of Prince Ruihuai Mianxin.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Prince Ruihuai Mianxin.

sentences.zh: 載瀾，奕脤第三子。

translations.literal: Zailan was Yicong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Zailan was Yicong's third son.

sentences.zh: 初封三等輔國將軍，再進封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as a third-rank auxiliary state general and later promoted to auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Initially created a third-rank auxiliary state general, he was later promoted to auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 以庇義和拳，奪爵，戍新疆。

translations.literal: For shielding the Boxers he was stripped of his title and banished to serve in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: For protecting the Boxers he was stripped of his title and sent into exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 載津，奕脤第五子。

translations.literal: Zaijin was Yicong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Zaijin was Yicong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 封二等鎮國將軍，加不入八分輔國公銜。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as a second-rank state-supporting general with the rank of auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: He was created a second-rank state-supporting general with the rank of an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 瑞懷親王綿忻，仁宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Ruihuai Mianxin was Emperor Renzong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruihuai Mianxin was Renzong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年，封瑞親王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing he was enfeoffed as Prince Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 24 he was created Prince Rui.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，命在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he was ordered to serve in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3 he was ordered to serve in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，薨，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year he died; he was given the posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the eighth year and received the posthumous name Huai.

sentences.zh: 子奕約甫晬，上命定親王奕紹檢察邸第官吏，內務府大臣敬徵治家政。

translations.literal: His son Yiyue had just reached one year; the emperor ordered Prince Ding Yishao to inspect the residence's officials, and Minister of the Imperial Household Jingzheng to manage the household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiyue was still an infant. The emperor ordered Prince Ding Yishao to inspect the household staff and Minister of the Imperial Household Jingzheng to supervise the domestic administration.

sentences.zh: 十月，奕約襲郡王，予半俸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yiyue inherited as prince of the commandery and was granted half stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yiyue succeeded to the commandery princedom with half a prince's stipend.

sentences.zh: 尋更名奕志。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter his name was changed to Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his name was changed to Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 三十年五月，薨，諡曰敏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirtieth year he died; he was given the posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the thirtieth year and received the posthumous name Min.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons.

sentences.zh: 賜綿忻福晉郡王半俸。

translations.literal: Mianxin's princess consort was granted half the stipend of a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: Mianxin's consort was granted half a commandery prince's stipend.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，福晉薨，复賜奕志福晉郡王半俸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the princess consort died; Yizhi's consort was again granted half the stipend of a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 the consort died, and Yizhi's consort was granted half a commandery prince's stipend in turn.

sentences.zh: 十年，命以惇親王子載漪為奕志後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Prince Dun's son Zaiyi was ordered made Yizhi's heir and inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zaiyi, son of Prince Dun, was named Yizhi's heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，大婚，命食貝勒全俸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, at the grand wedding, he was ordered granted a beile's full stipend.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand wedding in Tongzhi 11 he was granted a beile's full stipend.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he was given princely rank of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 15 he was granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 十九年九月，授為御前大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the nineteenth year he was appointed an imperial presence minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the nineteenth year he was appointed minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進封端郡王。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was advanced to Prince Duan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Prince Duan of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 循故事，宜仍舊號；

translations.literal: According to precedent, he should have kept the old title;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent he should have kept the old title;

sentences.zh: 更曰端者，述旨誤，遂因之。

translations.literal: The change to "Duan" was due to an error in transcribing the imperial will, and the name was retained.
translations.idiomatic: The change to "Duan" came from a clerical error in transcribing the imperial will, and the mistaken title stuck.

sentences.zh: 載漪福晉，承恩公桂祥女，太后侄也。

translations.literal: Zaiyi's princess consort was a daughter of the Duke of Enlargement Guixiang and a niece of the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiyi's consort was a daughter of Duke of Enlargement Guixiang and the empress dowager's niece.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，太后復訓政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed control of the government.

sentences.zh: 二十五年正月，賜載漪子溥？

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year Zaiyi's son Pujun was granted
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year Zaiyi's son Pujun was granted

sentences.zh: 頭品頂帶。

translations.literal: a first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: a first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上承太后命，溥？

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the empress dowager's order conveyed through the emperor, Pujun
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, acting on the empress dowager's order, the emperor had Pujun

sentences.zh: 入為穆宗後，號「大阿哥」，命在弘德殿讀書，以承恩公尚書崇綺、大學士徐桐為之傅。

translations.literal: entered as heir to Emperor Muzong, with the title "Great Heir Apparent," and was ordered to study in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, with the Duke of Enlargement and Minister Chongqi and Grand Secretary Xu Tong appointed as his tutors.
translations.idiomatic: adopted as heir to Emperor Tongzhi, given the title "Great Heir Apparent," and assigned to study in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue under Duke of Enlargement and Minister Chongqi and Grand Secretary Xu Tong as tutors.

sentences.zh: 明年元旦，大高殿、奉先殿行禮，以溥？

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the following year, when rites were performed at the Hall of Great Height and the Hall of Ancestors, Pujun was sent
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the following year, when rites were held at the Hall of Great Height and the Hall of Ancestors, Pujun stood in

sentences.zh: 代。

translations.literal: in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 都下流言將下詔禪位，大學士榮祿與慶親王奕劻以各國公使有異同，諫止。

translations.literal: Rumors spread in the capital that an edict of abdication would be issued. Grand Secretary Ronglu and Prince Qing Yikuang, citing disagreement among the foreign ministers, remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors swept the capital that an abdication edict was imminent. Grand Secretary Ronglu and Prince Qing Yikuang argued that the foreign ministers were divided on the matter and persuaded the court to abandon the plan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，義和拳亂起，載漪篤信之，以為義民，亂遂熾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer Rebellion broke out. Zaiyi believed in it fervently, treated the Boxers as righteous people, and the disorder then flared.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising erupted. Zaiyi embraced it wholeheartedly, hailed the Boxers as loyal patriots, and the turmoil swiftly spread.

sentences.zh: 五月，命充總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was appointed a minister in charge of affairs with all nations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was appointed minister for the management of foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 義和拳擊殺日本使館書記杉山彬，复及德國使臣克林德，圍攻東交民巷使館。

translations.literal: The Boxers killed Sugiyama Akira, secretary of the Japanese legation, and also the German minister Klemens von Ketteler, and besieged the legation quarter in the Eastern Precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxers murdered Sugiyama Akira, secretary at the Japanese legation, and the German minister Baron von Ketteler, then laid siege to the legation quarter in Dongjiaomin Lane.

sentences.zh: 八月，諸國聯軍自天津逼京師，上奉太后出狩，載漪及溥？

translations.literal: In the eighth month the allied armies of the foreign powers advanced from Tianjin on the capital. The emperor accompanied the empress dowager on a hunting tour to the west; Zaiyi and Pujun
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the allied armies pressed toward the capital from Tianjin. The emperor accompanied the empress dowager on flight to the west; Zaiyi and Pujun

sentences.zh: 皆從。

translations.literal: both followed.
translations.idiomatic: went with them.

sentences.zh: 次大同，命載漪為軍機大臣，未踰月罷。

translations.literal: When they halted at Datong, Zaiyi was appointed a Grand Councilor; before a month had passed he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At Datong, Zaiyi was appointed to the Grand Council, but was removed less than a month later.

sentences.zh: 命奕劻與大學士李鴻章議和，諸國目載漪為首禍。

translations.literal: Yikuang and Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang were ordered to negotiate peace. The foreign powers regarded Zaiyi as the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Yikuang and Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang were charged with peace negotiations. The foreign powers singled out Zaiyi as the principal instigator.

sentences.zh: 十二月，奪爵，戍新疆。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month his title was stripped and he was banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was deprived of his rank and exiled to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 二十七年十月，上奉太后還京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year the emperor accompanied the empress dowager back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-seventh year the emperor and the empress dowager returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 次開封，諭：「載漪縱義和拳，獲罪祖宗，其子溥？

translations.literal: When they halted at Kaifeng, an edict declared: "Zaiyi indulged the Boxers and has offended our ancestors. His son Pujun
translations.idiomatic: At Kaifeng an edict was issued: "Zaiyi unleashed the Boxers and has sinned against the imperial ancestors. His son Pujun

sentences.zh: 不宜膺儲位，廢'大阿哥'名號。」

translations.literal: is unfit to hold the position of heir; the title 'Great Heir Apparent' is abolished."
translations.idiomatic: is unworthy of the succession; the title 'Great Heir Apparent' is revoked."

sentences.zh: 賜公銜俸，歸宗。

translations.literal: He was granted the stipend of a duke and returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a duke's stipend and sent back to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 二十八年六月，別以醇賢親王奕枻子鎮國公載洵為奕志後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year, separately, Zai Xun, state duke and son of Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan, was made heir to Yizhi and inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year, Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan's son, State Duke Zai Xun, was adopted as Yizhi's heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 宣統間，為海軍部尚書。

translations.literal: During the Xuantong reign he served as minister of the navy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuantong era he served as minister of the navy.

sentences.zh: 改海軍部大臣，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: The post was changed to minister of the navy department, and he was granted the rank of prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of the navy department and granted the rank of commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 惠端親王綿愉，仁宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Huiduan Mianyu was Emperor Renzong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huiduan Mianyu was Renzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十五年七月，宣宗即位，封惠郡王，在內廷行走，上書房讀書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, when Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince Hui of the commandery, ordered to serve in the inner court, and to study in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne in the seventh month of Jiaqing 25, Mianyu was created Prince Hui of the commandery, assigned to the inner court, and set to his studies in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 故事，親、郡王未及歲，食半俸。

translations.literal: By precedent, princes of the first and second rank who had not yet reached the age of majority received half stipend.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, princes of the first and second rank who had not yet come of age received half pay.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，命食全俸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he was ordered to receive full stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 he was granted full stipend.

sentences.zh: 十九年，進親王。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was advanced to prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to prince of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，諭：「惠親王為朕叔父，內廷召對及宴賚賞賜宜免叩拜，章奏免書名。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, an edict declared: "Prince Hui is my uncle. At imperial audiences and banquets in the inner court he should be excused from kneeling and bowing, and in memorials he need not sign his name."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, an edict declared: "Prince Hui is my uncle. At inner-court audiences and at imperial banquets and grants he shall be excused from kneeling and bowing, and need not sign his name on memorials."

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，賜御用龍褂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was granted an imperial dragon jacket for court use.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 3 he was granted an imperial dragon jacket.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全之徒北擾近畿，命為奉命大將軍，頒銳捷刀，統健銳、火器、前鋒、護軍、巡捕諸營，及察哈爾兵，哲里木、卓索圖、昭烏達東三盟蒙古兵，與科爾沁郡王僧格林沁督辦防剿。

translations.literal: When Hong Xiuquan and his followers raided the northern approaches to the capital, Mianyu was appointed general-in-chief by imperial command, presented with a sharp campaign saber, and put in command of the Elite, Firearms, Vanguard, Guard, and Patrol battalions, Chahar troops, and Mongol forces of the eastern three leagues of Jirem, Josutu, and Juu Uda, jointly supervising defense and suppression with Prince of the Commandery of Horqin Sengge Rinchen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan's forces threatened the capital region from the north, Mianyu was appointed general-in-chief by imperial command, given a campaign saber, and placed over the Elite, Firearms, Vanguard, Guard, and Patrol battalions, Chahar troops, and Mongol levies from the eastern leagues of Jirem, Josutu, and Juu Uda, sharing command of defense and suppression with Prince of Horqin Sengge Rinchen.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁出駐涿州，綿愉留京師。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen went out to encamp at Zhuozhou; Mianyu remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen took the field at Zhuozhou while Mianyu stayed in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 九月，會奏頒行銀錢鈔法。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he jointly memorialized to promulgate regulations on silver, cash, and banknotes.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he joined in memorializing for the promulgation of new regulations on silver, cash, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 時秀全兵至深州，請發哲里木盟馬隊一千及熱河、古北口兵各五百赴涿州助防；

translations.literal: At the time Xiuquan's army had reached Shenzhou. He requested that one thousand cavalry from the Jirem League and five hundred troops each from Rehe and Gubeikou be sent to Zhuozhou to assist in defense;
translations.idiomatic: With Xiuquan's army at Shenzhou, he requested a thousand Jirem cavalry and five hundred troops each from Rehe and Gubeikou to reinforce Zhuozhou;

sentences.zh: 復奏請發蒙古兵三千，以德勒克色楞為將，督兵進擊。

translations.literal: he further memorialized requesting three thousand Mongol troops under Delikeseleng as commander to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: and further requested three thousand Mongol troops under Delikeseleng to take the field and attack.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，命朝會大典外悉免叩拜。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was ordered to be excused from kneeling and bowing at all audiences except the great court ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he was excused from kneeling and bowing at all audiences save the major court ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尋與恭親王奕訢、定郡王載銓疏請鑄鐵錢為大錢輔，上令王詳議以行。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Prince Gong Yixin and Prince Ding of the commandery Zaiquan, he memorialized requesting that iron cash be cast as a supplement to large-value coins. The emperor ordered the prince to deliberate in detail and implement the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Prince Gong Yixin and Prince Ding Zaiquan in memorializing to cast iron cash as a supplement to large-denomination coins. The emperor ordered Mianyu to study the proposal in detail and put it into effect.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，北路肅清，行凱撤禮，上奉命大將軍印。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year the northern route was pacified. Victory rites of withdrawal were performed, and the emperor received the seal of general-in-chief by command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year the northern front was cleared. After the victory withdrawal ceremony, the emperor took back the seal of general-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以鑄鐵錢有效，下宗人府議敘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, because casting iron cash had proved effective, the matter was referred to the Imperial Clan Court for merit assessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, with the iron-cash policy judged a success, the case was sent to the Imperial Clan Court for commendation.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，以奏保耆英，罷中正殿、雍和宮諸職任。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, for having recommended Qiying in a memorial, he was removed from his posts at the Zhongzheng Hall and Yonghe Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was stripped of his duties at the Zhongzheng Hall and Yonghe Temple for having recommended Qiying.

sentences.zh: 九年，罷鐵錢局。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the iron-cash bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the iron-cash bureau was shut down.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，英、法二國兵至天津，命至通州與僧格林沁辦防，並諭綿愉及怡親王載垣、鄭親王端華、尚書肅順、軍機大臣等籌商交涉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, when British and French troops reached Tianjin, he was ordered to Tongzhou to organize defenses with Sengge Rinchen. Mianyu, Prince Yi Zaiyuan, Prince Zheng Duhua, Minister Sushun, the Grand Councilors, and others were also instructed to consult on negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year, as British and French forces reached Tianjin, he was sent to Tongzhou to organize defenses with Sengge Rinchen. Mianyu, Prince Yi Zaiyuan, Prince Zheng Duhua, Minister Sushun, and the Grand Councilors were also ordered to deliberate on diplomatic handling.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，穆宗典學，太后以綿愉行輩最尊，品行端正，命在弘德殿專司督責，並令王子奕詳、奕詢伴讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, when Emperor Muzong began his formal studies, the empress dowager, considering Mianyu the most senior in rank and upright in conduct, ordered him to supervise exclusively in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue, and directed the princes Yixiang and Yixun to study alongside the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2, when Emperor Tongzhi began his studies, the empress dowager—judging Mianyu the most senior in rank and of upright character—assigned him to supervise the emperor in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and had Princes Yixiang and Yixun attend as study companions.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，薨，上親臨奠，賜銀五千治喪，諡曰端。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year he died. The emperor attended the obsequies in person, granted five thousand taels of silver for the funeral, and gave the posthumous title Duan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the third year. The emperor attended the funeral in person, granted five thousand taels for the rites, and posthumously named him Duan.

sentences.zh: 子六，有爵者三：奕詳、奕詢、奕謨。

translations.literal: He had six sons; three held titles: Yixiang, Yixun, and Yimo.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons, three of whom held noble rank: Yixiang, Yixun, and Yimo.

sentences.zh: 奕詳，綿愉第五子。

translations.literal: Yixiang was Mianyu's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yixiang was Mianyu's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 賜三眼孔雀翎，進鎮國公，襲郡王。

translations.literal: He was granted a three-eyed peacock feather, advanced to state duke, and inherited as prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He received a three-eyed peacock feather, was promoted to state duke, and succeeded to the commandery princedom.

sentences.zh: 穆宗大婚，加親王銜。

translations.literal: At Emperor Muzong's grand wedding he was granted the rank of prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Tongzhi's grand wedding he was granted the rank of prince of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命食親王俸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to receive a prince's stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was granted a prince's stipend.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年十月，太后萬壽，命食親王全俸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Guangxu, on the empress dowager's birthday, he was ordered to receive a prince's full stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Guangxu 10, for the empress dowager's birthday, he was granted a prince's full stipend.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year he was appointed an inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eleventh year he was appointed minister of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，薨，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year he died; he was given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the twelfth year and received the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子載潤，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Zai Run inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zai Run succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 奕詢，綿愉第四子。

translations.literal: Yixun was Mianyu's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yixun was Mianyu's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封不入八分輔國公，進封鎮國公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges and later advanced to state duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created an auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges and later promoted to state duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，以愉恪郡王允潖五世孫載澤為後，襲輔國公，進鎮國公，加貝子銜。

translations.literal: He died without a son. Yunbi, prince of the commandery of Yu Ke, was made his heir in the fifth generation through Zai Ze, who inherited as auxiliary state duke, was advanced to state duke, and granted the rank of beizi.
translations.idiomatic: He died without heirs. Zai Ze, fifth-generation descendant of Prince Yu Ke Yunbi, was adopted as his successor, succeeded as auxiliary state duke, was promoted to state duke, and granted the rank of beizi.

sentences.zh: 光緒末，授度支部尚書。

translations.literal: At the end of the Guangxu reign he was appointed minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangxu era he was appointed minister of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 奕謨，綿愉第六子。

translations.literal: Yimo was Mianyu's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yimo was Mianyu's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 初封不入八分鎮國公，再進封貝子，加貝勒銜。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as a state duke outside the Eight Privileges, then advanced to beizi and granted the rank of beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created a state duke outside the Eight Privileges, then promoted to beizi and granted the rank of beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，以醇賢親王奕枻孫溥佶為後，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: He died. Puji, grandson of Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan, was made his heir and inherited as state duke.
translations.idiomatic: He died without heirs. Puji, grandson of Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan, was adopted as his successor and succeeded as state duke.

sentences.zh: 宣宗九子：孝全成皇后生文宗，孝靜成皇后生順和郡王奕綱、慧質郡王奕繼、恭忠親王奕訢，莊順皇貴妃生醇賢親王奕譞、鍾端郡王奕詥、孚敬郡王奕譓，和妃納喇氏生隱志郡王奕緯，祥妃鈕祜祿氏生惇勤親王奕誴。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had nine sons: Empress Xiaquan Cheng bore Emperor Wenzong; Empress Xiaojing Cheng bore Prince Shunhe of the commandery Yigang, Prince Huizhi of the commandery Yiji, and Prince Gongzhong Yixin; Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun bore Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan, Prince Zhongduan of the commandery Yihe, and Prince Fujing of the commandery Yihui; Consort He of the Nara clan bore Prince Yinzhi of the commandery Yiwei; Consort Xiang of the Niuhuru clan bore Prince Dunqin Yikui.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had nine sons: Empress Xiaquan Cheng bore Wenzong; Empress Xiaojing Cheng bore Princes Yigang of Shunhe, Yiji of Huizhi, and Yixin of Gongzhong; Imperial Noble Consort Zhuangshun bore Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan, Prince Yihe of Zhongduan, and Prince Yihui of Fujing; Consort He of the Nara clan bore Prince Yiwei of Yinzhi; and Consort Xiang of the Niuhuru clan bore Prince Yikui of Dunqin.

sentences.zh: 奕誴出為惇恪親王綿愷後。

translations.literal: Yikui was given out as heir to Prince Dunke Mian Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Yikui was adopted as heir to Prince Dunke Mian Kai.

sentences.zh: 隱志郡王奕緯，宣宗第一子。

translations.literal: Prince Yinzhi of the commandery Yiwei was Emperor Xuanzong's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yinzhi Yiwei was Xuanzong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 24 he was created beile.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年四月，薨，以皇子例治喪，進封隱志貝勒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eleventh year of Daoguang he died. He was buried by the rites prescribed for an imperial son and posthumously advanced to beile of Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Daoguang 11. He was buried with the rites due an imperial son and posthumously advanced to Beile of Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，進郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was advanced to prince of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, he was posthumously promoted to commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 無子，以貝勒綿懿子奕紀為後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: He had no son. Yiji, son of Beile Mianyi, was made his heir and inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons. Yiji, son of Beile Mianyi, was adopted as his heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恭勤。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Gongqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Gongqin.

sentences.zh: 子溥倫，襲貝子，進貝勒；

translations.literal: His son Pulun inherited as beizi and was advanced to beile;
translations.idiomatic: His son Pulun succeeded as beizi and was later promoted to beile;

sentences.zh: 溥侗，授一等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Putong was appointed a first-rank state-supporting general.
translations.idiomatic: Putong was made a first-rank state-supporting general.

sentences.zh: 順和郡王奕綱，宣宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Shunhe of the commandery Yigang was Emperor Xuanzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shunhe Yigang was Xuanzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 二歲，殤。

translations.literal: At two years of age he died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at the age of two.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，進封諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, he was posthumously ennobled and given a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 慧質郡王奕繼，宣宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Huizhi of the commandery Yiji was Emperor Xuanzong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huizhi Yiji was Xuanzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 三歲，殤。

translations.literal: At three years of age he died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，追封諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, he was posthumously ennobled and given a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 恭忠親王奕訢，宣宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Gongzhong Yixin was Emperor Xuanzong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gongzhong Yixin was Xuanzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 與文宗同在書房，肄武事，共制槍法二十八勢、刀法十八勢，宣宗賜以名，槍曰「棣華協力」，刀曰「寶鍔宣威」，並以白虹刀賜奕訢。

translations.literal: He studied in the same schoolroom as Emperor Wenzong and trained in military arts. Together they devised twenty-eight spear forms and eighteen saber forms. Emperor Xuanzong bestowed names upon them: the spear was called "Dihua Xieli" and the saber "Baoe Xuanwei." He also granted Yixin the White Rainbow Saber.
translations.idiomatic: He studied alongside Wenzong and trained in the martial arts. Together they devised twenty-eight spear techniques and eighteen saber techniques. Xuanzong named them: the spear "Dihua Xieli" and the saber "Baoe Xuanwei." He also bestowed on Yixin the White Rainbow Saber.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，封為恭親王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, he was created Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年四月，分府，命仍在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Xianfeng he was granted a separate establishment but ordered to continue serving in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xianfeng 2 he was given his own establishment but ordered to remain in inner-court service.

sentences.zh: 內大臣辦理巡防，命仍佩白虹刀。

translations.literal: As an inner minister he managed patrol defense and was ordered to continue wearing the White Rainbow Saber.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed inner minister to manage patrol defense, he was permitted to continue wearing the White Rainbow Saber.

sentences.zh: 十月，全在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he entered service as a Grand Councilor with senior standing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was assigned to the Grand Council as a senior councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，迭授都統、右宗正、宗令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was successively appointed banner general, right clan director, and clan director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was successively appointed banner general, right clan director, and clan director.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，以畿輔肅清，予優敘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, because the capital region had been pacified, he was granted special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, with the capital region pacified, he received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 七月，孝靜成皇后崩，上責王禮儀疏略，罷軍機大臣、宗令、都統，仍在內廷行走，上書房讀書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Empress Xiaojing Cheng died. The emperor blamed the prince for negligence in ritual observance, removed him as Grand Councilor, clan director, and banner general, and ordered him to continue in the inner court and to study in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Empress Xiaojing Cheng died. The emperor faulted Yixin for lax observance of mourning rites, stripped him of his posts on the Grand Council, as clan director, and as banner general, and ordered him back to the inner court and the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，复授都統。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was again appointed banner general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he was reappointed banner general.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed an inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was appointed minister of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，英吉利、法蘭西兵逼京師，上命怡親王載垣、尚書穆廕與議和，誘執英使巴夏禮，與戰，師不利。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year, when British and French troops pressed on the capital, the emperor ordered Prince Yi Zaiyuan and Minister Muyin to negotiate peace. They lured and seized the British envoy Harry Parkes; battle followed, and the army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the tenth year, as British and French forces closed on the capital, the emperor ordered Prince Yi Zaiyuan and Minister Muyin to treat for peace. They seized the British envoy Harry Parkes by deception; fighting ensued, and the Qing forces were defeated.

sentences.zh: 文宗幸熱河，召回載垣、穆廕，授王欽差便宜行事全權大臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong went to Rehe. Zaiyuan and Muyin were recalled, and the prince was appointed imperial commissioner with full discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong fled to Rehe. Zaiyuan and Muyin were recalled, and Yixin was appointed imperial commissioner with full plenipotentiary authority.

sentences.zh: 王出駐長辛店，奏請飭統兵大臣激勵兵心，以維大局。

translations.literal: The prince went out to encamp at Changxindian and memorialized requesting that the commanding generals be ordered to rouse the troops' morale so as to sustain the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin took the field at Changxindian and memorialized urging the commanding generals to rally their troops and hold the line.

sentences.zh: 克勤郡王慶惠等奏釋巴夏禮，趣王入城議和。

translations.literal: Prince Keqin Qinghui and others memorialized to release Parkes and urged the prince to enter the city to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Keqin Qinghui and others memorialized for Parkes's release and pressed Yixin to enter the city to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 英、法兵焚圓明園。

translations.literal: British and French troops burned the Old Summer Palace.
translations.idiomatic: British and French forces burned the Yuanming Yuan.

sentences.zh: 豫親王義道等奏啟城，許英、法兵入。

translations.literal: Prince Yu Yidao and others memorialized to open the gates and allow British and French troops to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu Yidao and others memorialized to open the gates and admit the British and French armies.

sentences.zh: 王入城與議和，定約，悉從英、法人所請，奏請降旨宣示，並自請議處。

translations.literal: The prince entered the city to negotiate peace and concluded a treaty, accepting all that the British and French requested. He memorialized requesting that an edict be issued to proclaim the terms, and asked that he himself be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin entered the city, negotiated peace, and signed a treaty accepting the British and French demands in full. He memorialized for an edict to promulgate the terms and asked that he be punished.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「恭親王辦理撫局，本屬不易。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "Prince Gong's handling of the pacification was inherently no easy matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Prince Gong's management of the settlement was bound to be difficult.

sentences.zh: 朕深諒苦衷，毋庸議處。」

translations.literal: I deeply understand your difficulties; no punishment need be considered."
translations.idiomatic: I understand your predicament fully; no disciplinary action is required."

sentences.zh: 十二月，奏通商善後諸事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he memorialized on matters of trade and post-settlement administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he memorialized on trade and post-treaty administration.

sentences.zh: 初設總理各國事務衙門，命王與大學士桂良、侍郎文祥領其事。

translations.literal: The Office for the Management of Affairs of All Nations was established for the first time, and the prince, together with Grand Secretary Guiliang and Vice Minister Wen Xiang, was ordered to direct it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen was established for the first time, with Yixin, Grand Secretary Guiliang, and Vice Minister Wen Xiang placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 王疏請訓練京師旗兵，並以吉林、黑龍江與俄羅斯相議練兵籌餉。

translations.literal: The prince memorialized requesting the training of banner troops in the capital, and that Jilin and Heilongjiang negotiate with Russia on troop training and fund raising.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin memorialized to drill the banner troops of the capital and proposed that Jilin and Heilongjiang negotiate with Russia on training troops and raising funds.

sentences.zh: 上命都統勝保議練京兵，將軍景淳等議練東三省兵。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Banner General Sheng Bao to deliberate on drilling the capital troops, and Generals Jing Chun and others to deliberate on drilling the troops of the three eastern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Banner General Sheng Bao to plan the drilling of capital troops and Generals Jing Chun and others to plan training for the Three Eastern Provinces.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，文宗崩，王請奔赴，兩太后召見，諭以贊襄政務王大臣載垣、端華、肅順等擅政狀。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year Emperor Wenzong died. The prince requested permission to hurry to the scene. The two empress dowagers summoned him and informed him of the way Grand Councilors for Assisting Government Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and others had usurped power.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year Wenzong died. Yixin asked leave to rush to the scene. The two empress dowagers received him and described how the regent princes Zaiyuan, Duhua, Sushun, and their faction had seized power.

sentences.zh: 穆宗侍兩太后奉文宗喪還京師，譴黜載垣等，授議政王，在軍機處行走，命王爵世襲，食親王雙俸，並免召對叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, attending the two empress dowagers, brought Wenzong's coffin back to the capital. Zaiyuan and the others were censured and removed. The prince was appointed Prince Regent, assigned to the Grand Council, granted hereditary princely rank, double prince's stipend, exemption from kneeling at audiences, and exemption from signing his name on memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Tongzhi, accompanying the two empress dowagers, returned Wenzong's coffin to Beijing. Zaiyuan and his allies were purged. Yixin was made Prince Regent and Grand Councilor, granted a hereditary princedom, double prince's stipend, and exemption from kneeling at audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 王堅辭世襲，尋命兼宗令、領神機營。

translations.literal: The prince firmly declined hereditary succession. Soon afterward he was ordered to serve concurrently as clan director and to command the Shenji Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin firmly declined the hereditary grant. He was soon also appointed clan director and given command of the Shenji Battalion.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，上就傅，兩太后命王弘德殿行走，稽察課程。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, when the emperor began formal instruction, the two empress dowagers ordered the prince to serve in the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and to inspect the course of study.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1, when the emperor began his formal schooling, the two empress dowagers assigned Yixin to the Hall of Illustrious Virtue to supervise the curriculum.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧克復。

translations.literal: In the third year, Jiangning was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Nanjing was recovered.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「恭親王自授議政王，於今三載。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "Since Prince Gong was appointed Prince Regent, three years have now passed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "Prince Gong has served as Prince Regent for three years now.

sentences.zh: 東南兵事方殷，用人行政，徵兵籌餉，深資贊畫，弼亮忠勤。

translations.literal: Southeastern military affairs are still pressing; in appointing men and administering government, raising troops and provisioning funds, we have relied deeply on your counsel—loyal and diligent in support.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting still fierce in the southeast, he had been indispensable in staffing the government, raising armies, and securing funds—steadfast and devoted in counsel.

sentences.zh: 加封貝勒，以授其子輔國公載澂，並封載濬輔國公、載瀅不入八分輔國公。」

translations.literal: He was promoted to beile rank and it was granted to his son, Assistant Prince of the Second Rank Zai Cheng; Zai Jun was also enfeoffed as Assistant Prince of the Second Rank, and Zai Ying as Assistant Prince of the Second Rank outside the Eight Privileges."
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to beile rank, which was transferred to his son Zai Cheng, already an assistant prince of the second rank; Zai Jun was also enfeoffed as assistant prince of the second rank, and Zai Ying as assistant prince of the second rank outside the Eight Privileges."

sentences.zh: 四年三月，兩太后諭責王信任親戚，內廷召對，時有不檢，罷議政王及一切職任。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, the two empress dowagers rebuked the prince for favoring kinsmen and for lapses of decorum during inner-court audiences, and removed him as Prince Regent and from all offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, the two empress dowagers censured Yixin for trusting relatives and for occasional breaches of propriety at inner-court audiences, stripping him of the regency and every other post.

sentences.zh: 尋以惇親王奕脤、醇郡王奕枻及通政使王拯、御史孫翼謀、內閣學士殷兆鏞、左副都御史潘祖廕、內閣侍讀學士王維珍、給事中廣誠等奏請任用，廣誠語尤切。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Prince Dun Yixun, Prince Chun Yixuan, Transmission Commissioner Wang Zheng, Censor Sun Yimou, Hanlin Academy Bachelor Yin Zhaoyong, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Pan Zuyin, Hanlin Reader Wang Weizhen, Supervising Secretary Guang Cheng, and others memorialized requesting his reinstatement; Guang Cheng's language was especially forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Dun, Prince Chun, Transmission Commissioner Wang Zheng, Censor Sun Yimou, Hanlin bachelor Yin Zhaoyong, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Pan Zuyin, Hanlin reader Wang Weizhen, Supervising Secretary Guang Cheng, and others petitioned for his return; Guang Cheng's words were especially urgent.

sentences.zh: 兩太后命仍在內廷行走，管理總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers ordered that he continue to serve in the inner court and direct the Office for the Management of Affairs of All Nations.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers ordered him to remain in inner-court service and to direct the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 王入謝，痛哭引咎，兩太后复諭：「王親信重臣，相關休戚，期望既厚，責備不得不嚴。

translations.literal: The prince entered to give thanks, weeping as he accepted blame. The two empress dowagers again decreed: "As a trusted senior minister, your fortunes are bound up with ours; our hopes for you are great, and rebuke must therefore be strict.
translations.idiomatic: The prince came in to give thanks, weeping as he took the blame upon himself. The two empress dowagers again decreed: "You are a trusted senior minister whose fate is tied to our own; our expectations are high, and censure must therefore be stern.

sentences.zh: 仍在軍機大臣上行走。」

translations.literal: You shall continue to serve as a Grand Councillor."
translations.idiomatic: You shall continue to serve on the Grand Council."

sentences.zh: 七年二月，西捻逼畿輔，命節制各路統兵大臣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, when the Western Nian bandits pressed on the capital region, he was ordered to coordinate all commanding generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year, as the Western Nian rebels threatened the capital region, he was placed in overall command of the field commanders.

sentences.zh: 授右宗正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，穆宗大婚，復命王爵世襲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, at Emperor Muzong's grand wedding, the hereditary princedom was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, at Emperor Tongzhi's grand wedding, the hereditary princedom was restored to him.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，穆宗親政，十三年七月，上諭責王召對失儀，降郡王，仍在軍機大臣上行走，並奪載澂貝勒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year Emperor Muzong took personal rule; in the seventh month of the thirteenth year the emperor rebuked the prince for impropriety at audience, demoted him to junior prince, retained him on the Grand Council, and stripped Zai Cheng of his beile rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year Tongzhi assumed personal rule; in the seventh month of the thirteenth year the emperor censured Yixin for impropriety at audience, demoted him to junior prince while keeping him on the Grand Council, and stripped Zai Cheng of his beile rank.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以兩太后命复親王世襲及載澂爵。

translations.literal: The next day, by order of the two empress dowagers, the hereditary prince's rank and Zai Cheng's title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, on the two empress dowagers' order, the hereditary princedom and Zai Cheng's title were restored.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上疾有間，於雙俸外復加賜親王俸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when the emperor's illness eased, he was granted a prince's stipend in addition to his double stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when the emperor's illness briefly improved, he was granted a prince's stipend on top of his double stipend.

sentences.zh: 旋復加劇，遂崩。

translations.literal: The illness soon worsened again, and the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The illness soon turned worse again, and the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，復命免召對叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, the prince was again exempted from kneeling at audiences and from signing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu succeeded, Yixin was again exempted from kneeling at audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，署宗令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he served as acting clan director.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 he served as acting Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十年，法蘭西侵越南，王與軍機大臣不欲輕言戰，言路交章論劾。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when France invaded Vietnam, the prince and the Grand Council were unwilling to speak rashly of war; censorial memorials poured in denouncing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as France invaded Vietnam, Yixin and the Grand Council were reluctant to speak lightly of war; memorials from the censorate and other remonstrators poured in denouncing them.

sentences.zh: 太后諭責王等委靡因循，罷軍機大臣，停雙俸。

translations.literal: The empress dowager rebuked the prince and the others for timidity and procrastination, removed them from the Grand Council, and suspended the double stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager rebuked Yixin and the others for weakness and delay, removed them from the Grand Council, and suspended the double stipend.

sentences.zh: 家居養疾。

translations.literal: He lived at home to convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to his residence to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，复雙俸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year the double stipend was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year the double stipend was restored.

sentences.zh: 自是國及甲數，歲時祀事賜神糕，節序輒有賞賚，以為常。

translations.literal: From then on, at each year's festivals and seasons, divine cakes were bestowed for seasonal sacrifices, and gifts were regularly sent at each solar term—this became customary.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the year's festivals came round, divine cakes were granted for seasonal rites, and gifts were regularly bestowed at each turn of the calendar—this became the norm.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本侵朝鮮，兵？

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Japan invaded Korea, and the military crisis intensified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, as Japan invaded Korea, the military crisis grew acute.

sentences.zh: 有慶屢增護事急，太后召王入見，復起王管理總理各國事務衙門，並總理海軍，會同辦理軍務，內廷行走；

translations.literal: As the crisis repeatedly worsened and matters grew urgent, the empress dowager summoned the prince for an audience and reinstated him to direct the Zongli Yamen, take general charge of the navy, jointly oversee military affairs, and serve in the inner court;
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened again and again, the empress dowager summoned Yixin and restored him to head the Zongli Yamen, take charge of the navy, jointly oversee military affairs, and serve in the inner court;

sentences.zh: 仍諭王疾未癒，免常川入直。

translations.literal: The edict also noted that his illness had not yet healed and exempted him from regular attendance on duty.
translations.idiomatic: The edict also noted that his illness had not yet healed and exempted him from daily attendance on duty.

sentences.zh: 尋又命王督辦軍務，節制各路統兵大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was also ordered to supervise military affairs and coordinate all commanding generals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also ordered to supervise military affairs and coordinate all field commanders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was appointed Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授宗令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed clan director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 王疾作，閏三月增劇，上奉太后三臨視，四月薨，年六十七。

translations.literal: The prince fell ill; in the intercalary third month his condition worsened; the emperor accompanied the empress dowager in three bedside visits; he died in the fourth month at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin fell ill; in the intercalary third month his condition worsened; the emperor accompanied the empress dowager on three bedside visits; he died in the fourth month at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上再臨奠，輟朝五日，持服十五日。

translations.literal: The emperor visited again to mourn, court business was suspended for five days, and mourning dress was observed for fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited again to mourn; court was suspended for five days and mourning dress observed for fifteen.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠，配享太廟，並諭：「王忠誠匡弼，悉協機宜，諸臣當以王為法。」

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Zhong, granted posthumous worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and an edict stated: "The prince was loyal in support and wholly attuned to the needs of the hour—all ministers should take him as their model."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Zhong, granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and an edict declared: "The prince served loyally and met every exigency—let all ministers take him as their model."

sentences.zh: 子四：載澂，貝勒加郡王銜，卒，諡果敏；

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zai Cheng, beile with the additional title of junior prince, died, posthumously titled Guomin;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zai Cheng, a beile with the additional rank of junior prince, who died and was posthumously titled Guomin;

sentences.zh: 載瀅，出為鍾端郡王奕硉後，襲貝勒，坐事奪爵歸宗；

translations.literal: Zai Ying, given out as heir to Prince Zhongduan Yixiu, inherited as beile, lost his rank for an offense and returned to his original clan;
translations.idiomatic: Zai Ying, adopted as heir to Prince Zhongduan Yixiu, inherited as beile, lost his rank for an offense, and returned to his birth clan;

sentences.zh: 載濬，與載瀅同時受封；

translations.literal: Zai Jun, enfeoffed at the same time as Zai Ying;
translations.idiomatic: Zai Jun, enfeoffed at the same time as Zai Ying;

sentences.zh: 載潢，封不入八分輔國公。

translations.literal: Zai Huang, enfeoffed as Assistant Prince of the Second Rank outside the Eight Privileges.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Huang, enfeoffed as assistant prince of the second rank outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 載澂、載濬、載潢皆前王卒。

translations.literal: Zai Cheng, Zai Jun, and Zai Huang all died before the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Cheng, Zai Jun, and Zai Huang all died before their father.

sentences.zh: 王薨，以載瀅子溥偉為載澂後，襲恭親王。

translations.literal: When the prince died, Pu Wei, son of Zai Ying, was made heir to Zai Cheng and succeeded as Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixin died, Pu Wei, son of Zai Ying, was made heir to Zai Cheng and succeeded as Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王奕譞，宣宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Chun the Worthy, Yixuan, was the seventh son of Emperor Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun the Worthy, Yixuan, was the seventh son of Emperor Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，封為醇郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong succeeded, he was enfeoffed as Prince Chun of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong succeeded, he was enfeoffed as Prince Chun of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年三月，分府，命仍在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Xianfeng, he was granted a separate residence but ordered to continue serving in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xianfeng 9 he was granted a separate residence but ordered to remain in inner-court service.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，諭免宴見叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong succeeded, he was exempted from kneeling at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded, he was exempted from kneeling at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 迭授都統、御前大臣、領侍神機營。

translations.literal: In succession he was appointed banner general, grand minister of the imperial presence, and commander of the Shenji Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he was appointed banner general, grand minister of the imperial presence, and commander of the Shenji Battalion.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，加親王銜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he received the additional rank of prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he received the additional rank of prince of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，兩太后命弘德殿行走，稽察課程。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the two empress dowagers assigned him to the Hall of Illustrious Virtue to inspect the course of study.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the two empress dowagers assigned him to the Hall of Illustrious Virtue to supervise the curriculum.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進封醇親王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Prince Chun of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Prince Chun of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 十二年，穆宗親政，罷弘德殿行走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Muzong took personal rule, his assignment to the Hall of Illustrious Virtue was ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Tongzhi assumed personal rule, his assignment to the Hall of Illustrious Virtue was ended.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，王奏兩太后，言：「臣侍從大行皇帝十有三年，昊天不弔，龍馭上賓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, the prince memorialized the two empress dowagers, saying: "I served the late emperor for thirteen years. Heaven was unkind; the dragon has ascended as guest on high.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu succeeded, Yixuan memorialized the two empress dowagers, saying: "I attended the late emperor for thirteen years. Heaven showed no mercy; the dragon carriage has ascended on high.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻遺容，五內崩裂。

translations.literal: Gazing upon his departed form, my innermost being is torn asunder.
translations.idiomatic: Beholding his departed face, my heart is torn apart.

sentences.zh: 忽蒙懿旨下降，擇定嗣皇帝，倉猝昏迷，罔知所措。

translations.literal: Suddenly receiving the empress dowager's decree to fix upon an heir to the throne, I was overwhelmed and confused, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly receiving the empress dowager's decree to choose the heir to the throne, I was stunned and bewildered, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 獨犯舊有肝疾，委頓成廢。

translations.literal: My chronic liver ailment alone has laid me prostrate and useless.
translations.idiomatic: My old liver ailment alone has left me prostrate and useless.

sentences.zh: 惟有哀懇矜全，許乞骸骨，為天地容一虛糜爵位之人，為宣宗成皇帝留一庸鈍無才之子。」

translations.literal: I can only plead piteously for mercy, begging permission to retire, that heaven and earth may suffer one who vainly occupies a princely seat, and that Emperor Xuanzong may be left one dull, talentless son."
translations.idiomatic: I can only plead piteously for mercy and beg leave to retire, that heaven and earth may tolerate one who vainly holds a princely rank, and that Emperor Xuanzong may be left one dull and untalented son."

sentences.zh: 兩太后下其奏王大臣集議，以王奏誠懇請罷一切職任，但令照料菩陀峪陵工，從之。

translations.literal: The two empress dowagers circulated his memorial to the princes and ministers for joint deliberation. Finding his words sincere, they requested that all his offices be removed and that he only supervise work on the tomb at Putuoyu; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The two empress dowagers circulated his memorial to the princes and ministers for joint deliberation. Finding his words sincere, they approved his request to be relieved of all offices and assigned him only to oversee work on the tomb at Putuoyu.

sentences.zh: 命王爵世襲，王疏辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was granted a hereditary princedom; he memorialized to decline; the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a hereditary princedom; he memorialized to decline; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，上在毓慶宮入學，命王照料。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu the emperor began his schooling in the Palace of Eternal Joy and the prince was ordered to supervise his care.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 2 the emperor began his schooling in the Palace of Eternal Joy and Yixuan was ordered to supervise his upbringing.

sentences.zh: 五年，賜食親王雙俸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was granted a double prince's stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was granted a double prince's stipend.

sentences.zh: 十年，恭親王奕訢罷軍機大臣，以禮親王世鐸代之，太后命遇有重要事件，與王商辦。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Prince Gong Yixin was removed from the Grand Council and Prince Li Shikuo replaced him, the empress dowager ordered that on important matters deliberation be held with the prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Prince Gong Yixin was removed from the Grand Council and Prince Li Shikuo replaced him, the empress dowager ordered that important matters be discussed with Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 時法蘭西侵越南，方定約罷兵，王議建海軍。

translations.literal: France was then invading Vietnam and had just concluded a treaty to end hostilities; the prince proposed the creation of a navy.
translations.idiomatic: France was then invading Vietnam and had just concluded a treaty to end hostilities; Yixuan proposed building a navy.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，設海軍衙門，命王總理，節制沿海水師，以慶郡王奕劻、大學士總督李鴻章、都統善慶、侍郎曾紀澤為佐。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year the Navy Yamen was established; the prince was made its director with authority over coastal naval forces, assisted by Prince Qing Yikuang, Grand Secretary and Governor-General Li Hongzhang, Banner General Shan Qing, and Vice Minister Zeng Jize.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year the Navy Yamen was established; Yixuan was made its director with authority over the coastal fleet, assisted by Prince Qing Yikuang, Grand Secretary and Governor-General Li Hongzhang, Banner General Shan Qing, and Vice Minister Zeng Jize.

sentences.zh: 定議練海軍自北洋始，責鴻章專司其事。

translations.literal: It was decided to build the navy beginning with the Northern Squadron, with Li Hongzhang put solely in charge.
translations.idiomatic: It was decided to build the navy beginning with the Northern Squadron, with Li Hongzhang put solely in charge.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，賜王與福晉杏黃轎，王疏辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year he and his consort were granted apricot-yellow sedan chairs; he memorialized to decline; this was denied.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year he and his consort were granted apricot-yellow sedan chairs; he memorialized to decline; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 鴻章經畫海防，於旅順開船塢，築砲台，為海軍收泊地。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang planned coastal defenses, opening a dockyard at Lüshun and building batteries as anchorages for the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang planned coastal defenses, opening a dockyard at Lüshun and building batteries to serve as naval anchorages.

sentences.zh: 北洋有大小戰艦凡五，輔以蚊船、雷艇，复購艦英、德，漸次成軍。

translations.literal: The Northern Squadron had five large and small warships in all, supplemented by gunboats and torpedo craft; ships were also purchased from Britain and Germany, and the fleet gradually took shape.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Squadron had five warships large and small, supplemented by gunboats and torpedo craft; additional vessels were purchased from Britain and Germany, and the fleet gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 五月，太后命王巡閱北洋，善慶從焉，會鴻章自大沽出海至旅順，歷威海、煙台，集戰艦合操，遍視礮台、船塢及新設水師學堂，十餘日畢事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the empress dowager ordered the prince to inspect the Northern Squadron; Shan Qing accompanied him. Li Hongzhang joined them from Dagu out to sea as far as Lüshun, passing Weihai and Yantai; warships were assembled for joint drills; batteries, dockyards, and the newly established naval academy were reviewed—the tour took more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the empress dowager ordered Yixuan to inspect the Northern Squadron; Shan Qing accompanied him. Li Hongzhang joined them from Dagu out to sea as far as Lüshun, passing Weihai and Yantai; warships were assembled for joint maneuvers; batteries, dockyards, and the newly established naval academy were reviewed—the tour took more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 王還京，奏獎諸將吏及所聘客將，請太后御書榜懸大沽海神廟。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, the prince memorialized to reward the officers and the foreign instructors hired, and requested that the empress dowager inscribe a plaque to be hung at the Sea God Temple at Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, Yixuan memorialized to reward the officers and the foreign instructors under hire, and requested that the empress dowager inscribe a plaque to hang at the Sea God Temple at Dagu.

sentences.zh: 太后命於明年歸政，王疏言：「皇帝甫逾志學，諸王大臣籥懇訓政，乞體念時艱，俯允所請，俟及二旬，親理庶務。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered that she would hand back power the following year. The prince memorialized: "The emperor has only just passed the age of fifteen; the princes and ministers earnestly plead for continued regency. I beg you to weigh the difficulties of the times and grant this request, deferring full personal rule until he reaches twenty.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered that she would restore power the following year. Yixuan memorialized: "The emperor has only just passed the age of fifteen; the princes and ministers earnestly plead for continued regency. I beg you to weigh the difficulties of the times and grant this request, deferring personal rule until he reaches twenty.

sentences.zh: 至列聖宮廷規制，遠邁前代。

translations.literal: As for the court institutions of the successive sage emperors, they far surpass those of earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The court institutions of the successive sage emperors far surpass those of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 將來大婚後，一切典禮，咸賴訓教。

translations.literal: After the future grand wedding, all ceremonial rites will depend on her instruction.
translations.idiomatic: After the future grand wedding, all ceremonial rites will depend on her instruction.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為諸事當先請懿旨，再於皇帝前奏聞，俾皇帝專心大政，承聖母之歡顏，免宮闈之劇務。

translations.literal: In my humble view, all matters should first be referred to the empress dowager for her decree, then reported to the emperor, so that he may devote himself to great affairs of state, enjoy his mother's smiles, and be spared the heavy burdens of inner-palace routine.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, all matters should first be referred to the empress dowager for her decree, then reported to the emperor, so that he may devote himself to great affairs of state, enjoy his mother's company, and be spared the heavy burdens of inner-palace routine.

sentences.zh: 此則非如臣生深宮者不敢知，亦不敢言也。」

translations.literal: This is something one who, like me, was born deep within the palace dares neither to know fully nor to speak of openly."
translations.idiomatic: This is something one who, like me, was born deep within the palace dares neither fully to know nor openly to speak of."

sentences.zh: 太后命毋庸議。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered that the matter need not be further discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered that the matter need not be further discussed.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，上親政。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year the emperor took personal rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year the emperor assumed personal rule.

sentences.zh: 四月，太后諭預備皇帝大婚，當力行節儉，命王稽察。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the empress dowager decreed that preparations for the emperor's grand wedding must be strictly economical and ordered the prince to inspect compliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the empress dowager decreed that preparations for the emperor's grand wedding must be strictly economical and ordered Yixuan to inspect compliance.

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，王奏：「太平湖賜第為皇帝發祥地。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year the prince memorialized: "The residence granted at Taiping Lake is the place where the emperor's fortune first arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year Yixuan memorialized: "The residence granted at Taiping Lake is where the emperor's destiny first took shape.

sentences.zh: 世宗以潛邸升為宮殿，高宗諭子孫有自籓邸紹承大統者，應用其例。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong rose from his princely residence it was converted into a palace; Emperor Gaozong decreed that descendants who succeed to the throne from a princedom should follow that precedent."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong rose from his princely residence it was converted into a palace; Emperor Gaozong decreed that descendants who succeed to the throne from a princedom should follow that precedent."

sentences.zh: 太后從之，别賜第，發帑十萬葺治。

translations.literal: The empress dowager agreed, granted another residence, and dispensed a hundred thousand taels for repairs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed, granted another residence, and dispensed a hundred thousand taels for repairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，大婚禮成，賜金桃皮鞘威服刀，增護治邸第未竟，復發帑六萬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, after the grand wedding was completed, he was granted a ceremonial saber with gold peach-wood scabbard; as repairs to the residence were not yet finished, another sixty thousand taels were dispensed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year, after the grand wedding was completed, he was granted a ceremonial saber with gold peach-wood scabbard; as repairs to the residence were not yet finished, another sixty thousand taels were dispensed.

sentences.zh: 並進封諸子：載灃鎮國公，載洵輔國公，載濤賜頭品頂帶、孔雀翎。

translations.literal: His sons were also promoted: Zai Feng as Defender Prince of the Third Rank, Zai Xun as Assistant Prince of the Second Rank, and Zai Tao granted the first-rank official's cap button and peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were also promoted: Zai Feng as defender prince of the third rank, Zai Xun as assistant prince of the second rank, and Zai Tao granted the first-rank cap button and peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二月，河道總督吳大澂密奏，引高宗御批通鑑輯覽，略謂：「宋英宗崇奉濮王，明世宗崇奉興王，其時議者欲改稱伯叔，實人情所不安，當定本生名號，加以徽稱」；

translations.literal: In the second month, Yellow River Director-General Wu Dacheng submitted a confidential memorial citing Emperor Gaozong's rescript on the Comprehensive Mirror, stating in summary: "When Emperor Yingzong of Song honored Prince Pu and Emperor Shizong of Ming honored Prince Xing, critics at the time wished to call them uncle and elder uncle—truly what human feeling could not accept; the style for the birth parents should be fixed and an honorific title added;"
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yellow River Director-General Wu Dacheng submitted a confidential memorial citing Emperor Gaozong's rescript on the Comprehensive Mirror, stating in summary: "When Emperor Yingzong of Song honored Prince Pu and Emperor Shizong of Ming honored Prince Xing, critics at the time wished to style them uncle and elder uncle—what human feeling could accept that? The style for the birth parents should be fixed and an honorific title added;"

sentences.zh: 且言：「在臣子出為人後，例得以本身封典貤封本生父母，況貴為天子，天子所生之父母，必有尊崇之典，請飭廷臣議醇親王稱號禮節。」

translations.literal: He also said: "When a subject is given out as heir to another line, he may by precedent extend his own honors to his birth parents; how much more when one is exalted as Son of Heaven—the birth parents of the Son of Heaven must have rites of honor; I request that the court ministers be ordered to deliberate on the style and ceremonial for Prince Chun."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When a subject is given out as heir to another line, he may by precedent extend his own honors to his birth parents; how much more the Son of Heaven—the birth parents of the emperor must have rites of honor. I request that the court ministers be ordered to deliberate on the style and ceremonial for Prince Chun."

sentences.zh: 特旨宣示。

translations.literal: The special edict was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The special edict was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 上即位逾年，王密奏：「臣見歷代繼承大統之君，推崇本生父母者，備載史書。

translations.literal: More than a year after the emperor's accession, the prince submitted a confidential memorial: "I have seen that emperors throughout history who succeeded to the great succession and honored their birth parents are fully recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year after the emperor's accession, Yixuan submitted a confidential memorial: "I have seen that emperors throughout history who succeeded to the great succession and honored their birth parents are fully recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 其中有適得至當者焉，宋孝宗不改子偁秀王之封是也。

translations.literal: Among them are cases that hit the mark exactly—Emperor Xiaozong of Song did not alter the enfeoffment of his birth father as Prince of Xiuyi is one.
translations.idiomatic: Some hit the mark exactly—Emperor Xiaozong of Song did not alter his birth father Zisheng's enfeoffment as Prince of Xiuyi is one such case.

sentences.zh: 有大亂之道焉，宋英宗之濮議、明世宗之議禮是也。

translations.literal: There are also paths to great disorder— the Pu controversy under Emperor Yingzong of Song and the Rites controversy under Emperor Shizong of Ming are examples.
translations.idiomatic: There are also paths to great disorder—the Pu controversy under Emperor Yingzong of Song and the Rites controversy under Emperor Shizong of Ming are examples.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼之儔，無足論矣。

translations.literal: Men like Zhang Cong and Gui E are not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhang Cong and Gui E are not worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 忠如韓琦，乃與司馬光議論牴牾，其故何歟？

translations.literal: Loyal as Han Qi was, he yet clashed in debate with Sima Guang—what was the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal as Han Qi was, he yet clashed in debate with Sima Guang—what was the reason?

sentences.zh: 蓋非常之事出，立論者勢必紛沓擾攘，乃心王室，不無其人；

translations.literal: When extraordinary matters arise, those who take positions are bound to swarm in confusion; among them are not lacking men whose hearts are loyal to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: When extraordinary matters arise, those who take positions are bound to swarm in confusion; among them are not lacking men whose hearts are loyal to the throne;

sentences.zh: 而以此為梯榮之具，迫其主以不得不視為莊論者，正復不少。
