translations.literal: yet there are also no few who use such matters as ladders to advancement, pressing their lord to treat their views as solemn doctrine whether he wishes to or not.
translations.idiomatic: yet there are also no few who use such matters as ladders to advancement, pressing their lord to treat their views as solemn doctrine whether he wishes to or not.

sentences.zh: 皇清受天之命，列聖相承，十朝一脈，詎穆宗毅皇帝春秋正盛，遽棄臣民。

translations.literal: The Great Qing received Heaven's mandate; successive sage emperors succeeded one another in a single line through ten reigns—how could Emperor Muzong the Resolute, in the prime of life, suddenly abandon his subjects?
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing received Heaven's mandate; successive sage emperors succeeded one another in a single line through ten reigns—how could Emperor Tongzhi the Resolute, in the prime of life, suddenly abandon his subjects?

sentences.zh: 皇太后以宗廟社稷為重，特命皇帝入承大統，复推恩及臣，以親王世襲罔替。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, placing the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain foremost, specially ordered the emperor to enter and succeed to the great succession, and extended grace even to me with a hereditary princedom in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, placing the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain foremost, specially ordered the emperor to enter and succeed to the great succession, and extended grace even to me with a hereditary princedom in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 渥叨異數，感懼難名。

translations.literal: I have received extraordinary favor beyond measure; gratitude and fear are beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: I have received extraordinary favor beyond measure; gratitude and fear are beyond words.

sentences.zh: 原不須更生過慮，惟思此時垂簾聽政，簡用賢良，廷議既屬執中，邪說自必潛匿。

translations.literal: Originally there was no need for further excessive worry; only I reflect that at this time, with the empress dowager ruling from behind the curtain, selecting the worthy and good, court deliberation being even-handed, heterodox opinions will of themselves lie hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Originally there was no need for further excessive worry; only I reflect that at this time, with the empress dowager ruling from behind the curtain and selecting the worthy and good, court deliberation being even-handed, heterodox opinions will of themselves lie hidden.

sentences.zh: 倘將來親政後，或有草茅新進，趨六年拜相捷徑，以危言故事聳動宸聰，不幸稍一夷猶，則朝廷滋多事矣。

translations.literal: If after personal rule begins some newly risen man from the wilds should take the shortcut of reaching chancellor within six years, using alarming precedents to startle the imperial ear, and the emperor should unfortunately waver even slightly, the court would become ever more troubled.
translations.idiomatic: If after personal rule begins some newly risen man from the wilds should take the shortcut of reaching chancellor within six years, using alarming precedents to startle the imperial ear, and the emperor should unfortunately waver even slightly, the court would become ever more troubled.

sentences.zh: 仰懇皇太后將臣此摺，留之宮中。

translations.literal: I humbly beg the empress dowager to keep this memorial of mine in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg the empress dowager to keep this memorial of mine in the palace.

sentences.zh: 俟皇帝親政，宣示廷臣世賞之由及臣寅畏本意，千秋萬載，勿再更張。

translations.literal: When the emperor assumes personal rule, let it be proclaimed to the court ministers the reason for the hereditary honors granted and my own intent of reverent fear, that for ten thousand generations it may never be reopened.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor assumes personal rule, let it be proclaimed to the court ministers the reason for the hereditary honors granted and my own intent of reverent fear, that for ten thousand generations it may never be reopened.

sentences.zh: 如有以治平、嘉靖之說進者，務目之為奸邪小人，立加屏斥。

translations.literal: If anyone should advance arguments like those of the Zhiping or Jiajing controversies, he must be marked out as a wicked and base man and immediately removed.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone should advance arguments like those of the Zhiping or Jiajing controversies, he must be marked out as a wicked and base man and immediately removed.

sentences.zh: 果蒙慈命嚴切，皇帝敢不欽遵，不但臣名節得以保全，而關乎君子小人消長之機者，實為至大且要。」

translations.literal: If I truly receive the empress dowager's stern command, how could the emperor fail to obey reverently? Not only would my own reputation and integrity be preserved, but what concerns the waxing and waning of gentlemen and petty men is truly of the greatest importance."
translations.idiomatic: If I truly receive the empress dowager's stern command, how could the emperor fail to obey reverently? Not only would my own reputation and integrity be preserved, but what concerns the waxing and waning of gentlemen and petty men is truly of the greatest importance."

sentences.zh: 太后如王言，留疏宮中。

translations.literal: The empress dowager did as the prince requested and kept the memorial in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager did as Yixuan requested and kept the memorial in the palace.

sentences.zh: 大澂疏入，諭曰：「皇帝入承大統，醇親王奕枻謙卑謹慎，翼翼小心，十餘年來，殫竭心力，恪恭盡職。

translations.literal: When Wu Dacheng's memorial was submitted, an edict stated: "The emperor has succeeded to the great succession. Prince Chun Yixuan is humble and cautious, treading with utmost care. For more than ten years he has exhausted heart and mind, reverently and respectfully fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Dacheng's memorial was submitted, an edict stated: "The emperor has succeeded to the great succession. Prince Chun Yixuan is humble and cautious, treading with utmost care. For more than ten years he has exhausted heart and mind, reverently and respectfully fulfilling his duties.

sentences.zh: 每優加異數，皆涕泣懇辭，前賜杏黃轎，至今不敢乘坐。

translations.literal: Whenever extraordinary honors were added, he wept and earnestly declined; the apricot-yellow sedan chair previously bestowed, he still dares not ride in to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever extraordinary honors were added, he wept and earnestly declined; the apricot-yellow sedan chair previously bestowed, he still dares not ride in to this day.

sentences.zh: 其秉心忠赤，嚴畏殊常，非徒深宮知之最深，實天下臣民所共諒。

translations.literal: His heart is utterly loyal and sincere, his reverence and awe beyond ordinary measure. Not only does the inner palace know this most deeply—it is understood throughout the realm by officials and common people alike.
translations.idiomatic: His heart is utterly loyal and sincere, his reverence and awe beyond ordinary measure. Not only does the inner palace know this most deeply—it is understood throughout the realm by officials and common people alike.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年正月初八日，王即有豫杜妄論一奏，請俟親政宣示，俾千秋萬載，勿再更張。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the first month of the first year of Guangxu, the prince submitted a memorial to forestall reckless talk in advance, asking that when personal rule begins it be proclaimed, that for ten thousand generations it never be reopened.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the first month of Guangxu 1, Yixuan submitted a memorial to forestall reckless talk in advance, asking that when personal rule begins it be proclaimed, that for ten thousand generations it never be reopened.

sentences.zh: 自古純臣居心，何以過此？

translations.literal: Since antiquity, what loyal subject's intent could surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, what loyal subject's intent could surpass this?

sentences.zh: 當歸政伊始，吳大澂果有此奏，特明白曉諭，並將王原奏發鈔，俾中外咸知賢王心事，從此可以共白。

translations.literal: At the very beginning of the restoration of personal rule, Wu Dacheng did indeed submit such a memorial. We therefore give clear instruction and circulate copies of the prince's original memorial, so that within and without the court all may know the virtuous prince's true intent—and from this the matter may be laid fully open.
translations.idiomatic: At the very beginning of the restoration of personal rule, Wu Dacheng did indeed submit such a memorial. The throne therefore gave clear instruction and circulated copies of Yixuan's original memorial, so that within and without the court all might know the virtuous prince's true intent—and from this the matter could be laid fully open.

sentences.zh: 闞名希寵之徒，更何所容其覬覦乎？」

translations.literal: What room remains for those who crave fame and fawn for favor to harbor designs?"
translations.idiomatic: What room remains for those who crave fame and fawn for favor to harbor designs?"

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，以上二十萬壽，增護軍十五、藍白甲五十，授載濤二等鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, on the occasion of the emperor's twentieth birthday, fifteen guardsmen and fifty blue-and-white armor-bearers were added, and Zaitao was appointed second-rank state-supporting general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year, on the occasion of the emperor's twentieth birthday, fifteen guardsmen and fifty blue-and-white armor-bearers were added, and Zaitao was created second-rank state-supporting general.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王疾作，上親詣視疾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the prince fell ill; the emperor went in person to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yixuan fell ill; the emperor went in person to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，王薨，年五十一。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai the prince died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai the prince died, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 太后臨奠，上詣邸成服。

translations.literal: The empress dowager came to pay last respects; the emperor went to the prince's residence to don mourning robes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager came to pay last respects; the emperor went to the prince's residence to don mourning robes.

sentences.zh: 定稱號曰皇帝本生考，稱本生考，遵高宗御批；

translations.literal: The title was fixed as the emperor's biological father; to call him biological father followed the Qianlong emperor's imperial annotation;
translations.idiomatic: The title was fixed as the emperor's biological father; to call him biological father followed the Qianlong emperor's imperial annotation;

sentences.zh: 仍原封，從王志也。

translations.literal: His original enfeoffment was preserved, in accordance with the prince's own wish.
translations.idiomatic: His original enfeoffment was preserved, in accordance with Yixuan's own wish.

sentences.zh: 諡曰賢，配享太廟。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Xian; he was granted a share in sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Xian and granted a share in sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣議：上持服期年，縞素、輟朝十一日；

translations.literal: Court ministers were ordered to deliberate: the emperor would observe mourning for one full year, wear white hemp, and suspend court for eleven days;
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers were ordered to deliberate: the emperor would observe mourning for one full year, wear white hemp, and suspend court for eleven days;

sentences.zh: 初祭、大祭，奉移前一日，親詣行禮，禦青長袍褂，摘纓；

translations.literal: for the initial and major sacrificial rites, on the day before the coffin was moved, he would go in person to perform the rites, wearing a blue long robe and jacket with the tassel of his hat removed;
translations.idiomatic: for the initial and major sacrificial rites, on the day before the coffin was moved, he would go in person to perform the rites, wearing a blue long robe and jacket with the tassel of his hat removed;

sentences.zh: 期年內禦便殿，用素服；

translations.literal: within the mourning year he would hold audience in the informal hall in plain garments;
translations.idiomatic: within the mourning year he would hold audience in the informal hall in plain garments;

sentences.zh: 葬以王，祭以天子，立廟班諱。

translations.literal: he would be buried with princely rites but sacrificed to with imperial rites, a temple would be established, and his name tabooed in the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: he would be buried with princely rites but sacrificed to with imperial rites, a temple would be established, and his name tabooed in the calendar.

sentences.zh: 十八年，葬京師西山妙高峰。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was buried at Miao Peak in the Western Hills outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was buried at Miao Peak in the Western Hills outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣統皇帝即位，定稱號曰皇帝本生祖考。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong emperor succeeded to the throne, the title was fixed as the emperor's biological grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuantong succeeded to the throne, the title was fixed as the emperor's biological grandfather.

sentences.zh: 子七：德宗，其第二子也；

translations.literal: He had seven sons: the Guangxu emperor was his second son;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Emperor Guangxu was his second son;

sentences.zh: 載洸，初封不入八分輔國公，進鎮國公；

translations.literal: Zaiguang was first enfeoffed as auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges, then promoted to state duke;
translations.idiomatic: Zaiguang was first created auxiliary state duke outside the Eight Privileges, then promoted to state duke;

sentences.zh: 載灃，襲醇親王，宣統皇帝即位，命為監國攝政王；

translations.literal: Zaifeng inherited the princedom of Chun; when the Xuantong emperor succeeded, he was appointed regent prince;
translations.idiomatic: Zaifeng inherited the princedom of Chun; when Emperor Xuantong succeeded, he was appointed regent prince;

sentences.zh: 載洵，出為瑞郡王奕志後；

translations.literal: Zaixun was adopted as heir to Prince Rui Yizhi;
translations.idiomatic: Zaixun was adopted as heir to Prince Rui Yizhi;

sentences.zh: 載濤，出為鍾郡王奕硉後。

translations.literal: Zaitao was adopted as heir to Prince Zhong Yilü.
translations.idiomatic: Zaitao was adopted as heir to Prince Zhong Yilü.

sentences.zh: 宣統間，載洵為海軍部大臣，載濤為軍諮府大臣，主軍政。

translations.literal: During the Xuantong reign Zaixun served as minister of the navy and Zaitao as minister of the military advisory council, both directing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuantong reign Zaixun served as minister of the navy and Zaitao as minister of the military advisory council, both directing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，並罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Xuantong 3 both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遜位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month [the emperor] abdicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the throne was abdicated.

sentences.zh: 鍾端郡王奕詥，宣宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Zhongduan Yigou was Emperor Daoguang's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhongduan Yigou was Emperor Daoguang's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，封為鍾郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianfeng succeeded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianfeng succeeded he was created Prince of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，命免宴見叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，分府，仍在內廷行走。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he was given a separate estate but continued to serve in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he was given a separate estate but continued to serve in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月，薨，諡曰端。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he died; his posthumous name was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tongzhi 7 he died; his posthumous name was Duan.

sentences.zh: 無子，以恭忠親王奕訢子載瀅為後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: Having no son, Prince Gong Yixin's son Zaiying was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, Prince Gong Yixin's son Zaiying was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵，歸宗。

translations.literal: Convicted of an offense, he was stripped of his title and returned to his original line.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of an offense, he was stripped of his title and returned to his original line.

sentences.zh: 又以醇賢親王奕枻子載濤為後，襲貝勒，加郡王銜。

translations.literal: Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan's son Zaitao was then adopted as heir, succeeded as beile, and given princely rank of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun the Worthy Yixuan's son Zaitao was then adopted as heir, succeeded as beile, and granted princely rank of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 孚敬郡王奕譓，宣宗第九子。

translations.literal: Prince Fujing Yihui was Emperor Daoguang's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fujing Yihui was Emperor Daoguang's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，封孚郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianfeng succeeded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianfeng succeeded he was created Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，命免宴見叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，分府，仍在內廷行走，命管樂部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he was given a separate estate, continued in the inner court, and put in charge of the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 3 he was given a separate estate, continued in the inner court, and put in charge of the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授內大臣，加親王銜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed grand minister of the imperial household and given the rank of full prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed grand minister of the imperial household and granted princely rank.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，復命免宴見叩拜、奏事書名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangxu succeeded he was again exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangxu succeeded he was again exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences and from signing memorials.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年二月，薨，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Guangxu he died; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Guangxu 3 he died; his posthumous name was Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子，以愉恪郡王允潖四世孫奕棟子載沛為後，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: Having no son, Prince Yu Ke Yunbi's fourth-generation descendant Yidong's son Zaibo was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: Having no son, Prince Yu Ke Yunbi's fourth-generation descendant Yidong's son Zaibo was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，又以奕瞻子載澍為後，襲貝勒，坐事奪爵歸宗；

translations.literal: When he died, Yizhan's son Zaishu was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile; convicted of an offense he was stripped of his title and returned to his original line;
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Yizhan's son Zaishu was adopted as heir and succeeded as beile; convicted of an offense he was stripped of his title and returned to his original line;

sentences.zh: 又以貝勒載瀛子溥伒為後，封貝子。

translations.literal: Beile Zaiying's son Puqi was then adopted as heir and enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Beile Zaiying's son Puqi was then adopted as heir and created beizi.

sentences.zh: 文宗二子：孝欽顯皇后生穆宗，玫貴妃徐佳氏生憫郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianfeng had two sons: Empress Xiaojuan Xian bore Emperor Tongzhi; Concubine Mei of the Xu clan bore the Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianfeng had two sons: Empress Xiaojuan Xian bore Emperor Tongzhi; Concubine Mei of the Xu clan bore the Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 憫郡王，生未命名，殤。

translations.literal: The Prince of Min was born without being given a personal name and died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Min was born without being given a personal name and died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，追封。

translations.literal: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi succeeded he was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：莊親王佐太祖建業，將出師，登壠而謀，策定馳而下，黃道周亟稱其驍勇；

translations.literal: The editors say: Prince Zhuang aided the Taizu emperor in founding the enterprise. About to take the field, he ascended a height to plan strategy; once the plan was settled he galloped down. Huang Daozhou repeatedly praised his fierce bravery;
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Prince Zhuang aided the Taizu emperor in founding the dynasty. As he prepared to march, he climbed a height to lay his plans; once they were set, he galloped down. Huang Daozhou praised his valor without stint;

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，諸子嗣業，未有成命，禮烈親王擁立太宗，親為扞禦邊圉，夏允彝以為行事何減聖賢。

translations.literal: When the Taizu emperor died the princes inherited the enterprise without a settled succession. Prince Lie Daishan raised the Taizong emperor to the throne and personally defended the frontier. Xia Yunyi held that his conduct was in no way inferior to that of sages.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu emperor died the princes inherited the enterprise without a settled succession. Prince Lie Daishan raised Hong Taiji to the throne and personally defended the frontier. Xia Yunyi held that his conduct was in no way inferior to that of sages.

sentences.zh: 蓋雄才讓德，雖在敵國，不能掩也。

translations.literal: Such is the way of great talent yielding to virtue—even in an enemy state it cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Talent of such magnitude yielding to virtue—even a hostile realm could not hide it.

sentences.zh: 睿忠親王手定中原，以致於世​​祖，求之前史，實罕其倫。

translations.literal: Prince Rui Dorgon personally secured the Central Plain down to the Shizu emperor's reign; searching through earlier history, his like is truly rare.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui Dorgon personally secured the Central Plain down to the Shunzhi emperor's reign; searching through earlier history, his like is truly rare.

sentences.zh: 徒以執政久，威福自專，其害肅武親王，相傳謂因師還賜宴拉殺之，又或謂還至郊外遇伏死，死處即今葬地。

translations.literal: Yet because he held power long and monopolized authority, in the harm he did to Prince Su Hooge—tradition has it that on returning from campaign he was strangled at a banquet given in his honor; others say he was ambushed and killed outside the city, the place of death being his present burial site.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he held power long and monopolized authority, in the harm he did to Prince Su Hooge—tradition has it that on returning from campaign he was strangled at a banquet given in his honor; others say he was ambushed and killed outside the city, the place of death being his present burial site.

sentences.zh: 傳聞未敢信，然其慘酷可概見矣。

translations.literal: One dares not fully credit such rumors, yet his brutality may be seen at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: The rumors cannot be fully credited, yet they reveal the cruelty of his rule.

sentences.zh: 身後蒙謗，僅乃得雪，亦有以取之也。

translations.literal: After death he was slandered and only belatedly vindicated—yet he had brought much of this upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was slandered and only belatedly vindicated—yet he had brought much of this upon himself.

sentences.zh: 聖祖遇諸宗人厚，遺詔猶以禮親王、饒餘親王子孫安全，拳拳在念。

translations.literal: The Kangxi emperor treated the imperial clansmen with generosity; even in his deathbed testament he gave anxious thought to the safety of the descendants of Princes Li and Raoyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi emperor treated the imperial clansmen with generosity; even in his deathbed testament he gave anxious thought to the safety of the descendants of Princes Li and Raoyu.

sentences.zh: 然當用兵時，諸王貝勒為帥，小違律必議罰，且不得以功掩。

translations.literal: Yet in time of war, when princes and beiles served as commanders, even slight breaches of military law were subject to punishment—and merit could not cover the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in time of war, when princes and beiles served as commanders, even slight breaches of military law were subject to punishment—and merit could not cover the offense.

sentences.zh: 義以行法，仁以睦親，固不相悖也。

translations.literal: Righteousness in enforcing the law and benevolence in nurturing kin are not at all incompatible.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness in enforcing the law and benevolence in nurturing kin are not at all incompatible.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，允禩、允禟之獄，世宗後亦悔之。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign the cases of Yunsi and Yuntang—the Yongzheng emperor came to regret them afterward.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign the cases of Yunsi and Yuntang—the Yongzheng emperor came to regret them afterward.

sentences.zh: 怡賢親王特馴謹，渥加寵榮，示非寡恩。

translations.literal: Prince Yixian was especially docile and cautious and received lavish favor—showing that [the emperor] was not devoid of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixian was especially docile and cautious and received lavish favor—showing that the emperor was not devoid of grace.

sentences.zh: 誠以尺布鬥粟，相逼笮過甚，恂勤郡王嘗握兵柄，非母弟亦豈得幸生耶？

translations.literal: Indeed, when brothers press each other as with 'a foot of cloth, a peck of grain,' the pressure can be excessive. Prince Xunqin Yinti once held military power—had he not been the emperor's uterine younger brother, could he have hoped to survive?
translations.idiomatic: Indeed, when brothers press each other as with 'a foot of cloth, a peck of grain,' the pressure can be excessive. Prince Xunqin Yinti once held military power—had he not been the Yongzheng emperor's uterine younger brother, could he have hoped to survive?

sentences.zh: 時去開國未遠，以尚武為家法，其失則獷。

translations.literal: The age was not far removed from the founding; martial prowess was the family code—its failing was harshness.
translations.idiomatic: The age was not far removed from the founding; martial prowess was the family code—its failing was harshness.

sentences.zh: 太宗屢諭諸子弟當讀書，愨厚公承其教，彬彬有東丹王之風。

translations.literal: The Taizong emperor repeatedly admonished the princes to study; Duke Kehou embraced his teaching and had the refined bearing of the Prince of Dongdan.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong emperor repeatedly admonished the princes to study; Duke Kehou embraced his teaching and had the refined bearing of the Prince of Dongdan.

sentences.zh: 高宗諸子多擅文學，尤以成哲親王為最，詞章書翰，無愧古人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's sons were widely versed in letters, Prince Cheng Zhi Yongrong foremost among them—his poetry and calligraphy did not shame the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong's sons were widely versed in letters, Prince Cheng Zhi Yongrong foremost among them—his poetry and calligraphy did not shame the ancients.

sentences.zh: 恭忠親王繼以起，綢繆宮府，定亂綏疆，罷不生懟，用不辭勞，有純臣之度焉。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Yixin rose in his turn, tending meticulously to palace and government, quelling disorder and pacifying the realm—never resentful when dismissed, never shirking when employed—he had the measure of a loyal minister indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Yixin rose in his turn, tending palace and government with meticulous care, quelling disorder and pacifying the realm—never resentful when dismissed, never shirking when employed—he had the bearing of a loyal minister through and through.

sentences.zh: 醇賢親王尊為本生親，乾乾翼翼，靡間初終，預絕治平、嘉靖之議，載在方策，彰彰邁前代遠甚。

translations.literal: Prince Chun the Worthy, honored as the emperor's biological kin, was diligent and cautious without break from first to last, forestalling in advance the Zhiping and Jiajing controversies—recorded in the official annals, far surpassing earlier ages in plainness for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chun the Worthy, honored as the emperor's biological kin, was diligent and cautious without break from first to last, forestalling in advance the Zhiping and Jiajing controversies—recorded in the official annals, his example far outshone anything in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 迨時移勢易，天方降割，乃以肺腑之親，寄腹心之重，漠然不知陰雨之已至，一發而不可復收。

translations.literal: But when times shifted and Heaven began to afflict the dynasty, those closest in blood were entrusted with the weight of state—yet remained oblivious that the storm had already gathered; once loosed, the catastrophe could not be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: But when times shifted and Heaven began to afflict the dynasty, flesh-and-blood kin were entrusted with the weight of the realm—yet remained oblivious that the storm had already gathered; once loosed, the catastrophe could not be recalled.

sentences.zh: 天歟人歟，亡也忽諸，尤足為後來之深鑑矣！

translations.literal: Heaven's will, or human failing—the collapse came in the blink of an eye, and stands as a stark warning for those who follow!
translations.idiomatic: Was it Heaven's decree, or human failing? The dynasty vanished almost overnight—a lesson that those who come after would do well to heed.
